shardiuss_excavation.hook: A cut-away of a Blackwood hillside held in scaffolds above a stepped Ayleid terrace, with ladders going down into pale-white stone.
shardiuss_excavation.rumour: They say the diggers at Shardiuss all quit on one day, paid in barrels instead of coin, and none will go near the pit.

notes.title: Foreman's Tally, Shardiuss
notes.author: Dorrel Ansgate
pages: Day 31. Sixty names read off the lintel, as the contract asks. At the sixtieth the lamps came on without oil and a voice answered from the cut. I have paid the men in wine as I was told and sent the rubbing to the gate at Alma Ruma. Do not read aloud. Do not say them.

notes.title: Lampwright's Census Page
notes.author: Lampwright Ilvaren
pages: Stone one: relit, Shardiuss. Stone two: Miscarcand's cold vault, relit by the third night. Stone three: Ne Salas pillar, pending. The cabal's instruction: light in order, do not skip. The order matters. Do not ask why; we have asked, and the answer was a silence like a held breath.

gate_of_alma_ruma.hook: A worn Alessian gate of white stone with a scroll-temple annex leaning against its flank, still ringed by a dry processional road.
gate_of_alma_ruma.rumour: The Alma Ruma annex has a ledger of names and the old priest there weeps when anyone asks to see the page that was cut out.

notes.title: Register of Unfreed Names
notes.author: Brother Hesperin
pages: Struck through: 11. Unstruck: 4,208. The page that held the Nibenay vintners was cut out in the year of my predecessor's death and the wine-house of Thalaras never answered my letters. I have kept the register open. The dead are not finished.

thalaras_winery.hook: A single-family cellar estate with a stone press, where the vines have grown over a flagstone floor that is, in fact, a lamp-hall roof.
thalaras_winery.rumour: The Thalaras cellar sells a wine that tastes like a memory. No one who drinks it will say whose.

notes.title: A Vintner's Last Letter
notes.author: Orsolya Thalaras
pages: To whoever holds the estate after me. Do not sell the oldest rows to the Count's steward. The vines drink from the vault, and the vault is full of names that the Warden keeps. Press them, bottle them, give each its day, but never let one be spoken whole at once. Miscarcand is only a door. We are the lock.

mist_mirror_refuge.hook: A hidden waterfall pool in the Nibenay valley that mirrors a different night sky from the one overhead, ringed in cut stones under the water.
mist_mirror_refuge.rumour: The pool at Mist Mirror shows the wrong stars. I do not go at night, and I do not go alone.

notes.title: The Pool Remembers
notes.author: unknown pilgrim
pages: ~Water lies still and the stars come down,~not ours, not ours, but some old town.~Each star a name, each name a flame,~each flame put out by a man who came.~Say it not aloud, say it not twice,~the pool will give you your price.

miscarcand.hook: A buried Ayleid city-vault of lit welkynd stone, tiered cisterns and bridges over drowned galleries.
miscarcand.rumour: Miscarcand's gate lamps burn blue when a name is read, and some say the dead there are waiting to be asked.

notes.title: The Cold Vault Lintel
pages: HERE LIES THE ACCOUNT OF THE UNNUMBERED. Whoever takes a plate takes a person. Whoever restores a plate restores a debt. The Warden counts, and the count will not be closed by force, only by name.

notes.title: A Lampwright's Letter
notes.author: Lampwright Ilvaren
pages: To Aelwyn at the Tower. Two stones lit and the vault at Miscarcand is awake: do not let the Warden count the names while the lamps are new. I have left a seal on the lintel. We proceed to Ne Salas. The dead are listening; keep your voice level.

lunar_fang_docks.hook: Rickety lake docks lit by a string of pale moonlamps, with a dozen boats that never leave and a single candle on the harbour-master's step.
lunar_fang_docks.rumour: The Lunar Fang boats don't fish the south reach any more. They light a candle and sit in the dark instead.

notes.title: Pinned to the Harbour Post
pages: To the brothers of the Candle. The man from Kvatch asked us to leave the sea-door unbarred for one night so the dead might walk home. We did. Do not light the candle again until we know what came through. If anyone asks, the docks were never ours.

notes.title: Boatman's Orders
notes.author: the Counting-House
pages: Night boats from the Lunar Fang dock to carry sealed ledgers to the Bitter Coast. No questions. No passengers. If a passenger is found aboard, the passenger is to be delivered to the master at the swamp-market, who will see that no harm comes to them. We pay in years.

dark_brotherhood_sanctuary_cyrodiil.hook: A hidden cellar sanctuary under a nondescript house on the Gold Coast, with a small crypt-warren, a communal hall and a locked inner coffin-room.
dark_brotherhood_sanctuary_cyrodiil.rumour: A house on the Gold Coast road has no windows and a smoke-hole that smells of fish. People cross the street.

notes.title: Contract: The Priest
notes.author: the Listener's scribe
pages: Target: Father Aldric Merenth of Kvatch. Fee: unpaid, client cannot be found. Note: the priest asked us to hold his last letter until the Candle came for it. No one has. File under unfinished. Do not open the coffin.

deepscorn_hollow.hook: A coastal cave with a drowned lower level, a moon-lit sink-hole and a bone-white hall that shows different rooms at different tides.
deepscorn_hollow.rumour: The Hollow's caves flood and empty twice a day. Folk say a candle burns down there that never goes out.

notes.title: A Survivor's Diary
notes.author: Wren of Kvatch
pages: They took us in because we could say where the Candle's keepers lived. We said. Now they ask for the one name I will not give: my brother's. He kept the book of the night the Gate opened. I tell them nothing. The tide is out. I light the candle.

kvatch_gate.hook: The burning crater edge where the Gate first opened, with a wrecked siege-tower, a plume of ash and a ring of lava glass.
kvatch_gate.rumour: At dusk the ash at the crater rises instead of falling. The masons say it is looking for someone.

notes.title: Prayer for a Latched Door
notes.author: the Ashen Candle
pages: Light the wick, close the door, and leave the latch alone. Let the drowned go home and let the burning stay out. We did not know the door had two sides. Forgive us the one we left on the latch.

weynon_priory.hook: A grey-stone cloister with a bell tower and an orchard on the Colovian slopes, where a single clapperless bell hangs from the orchard wall.
weynon_priory.rumour: The priory's bell rings once at night with no hand on it. The brothers say to leave it be.

notes.title: Brother Jaren's Notes
notes.author: Brother Jaren
pages: Seven bells: Weynon, Sentinel's ridge, Bruma chapel, the Cloud Ruler cloister, Frostcrag, a small bell at the barrow, and Sancre Tor. A woman in grey took the Weynon clapper and left a donation. She says she keeps a vigil older than the Empire. I did not like her smile.

the_sentinel.hook: A lone statue guardian on a ridge above the Valus road, hand raised against something no traveller can see.
the_sentinel.rumour: Wind drops dead at the foot of the Sentinel, and the ravens won't land on it.

notes.title: Plinth Inscription
pages: KEEP THE VIGIL. Whoever raises a bell on this ridge lets something hear. Whoever takes one down keeps the dark in its place. Sentinel, watch the seven. Sentinel, watch the door.

cloud_ruler_temple.hook: The Blades' cliff keep above the cloud line, with banners, wind and a rope bridge over the whole Jerall range.
cloud_ruler_temple.rumour: The Cloud Ruler cloister has a row of bells that don't ring, and a woman in grey who polishes them.

notes.title: The Long Watch
notes.author: Archivist Sevrin Dal
pages: We hold the seven. Four are in the high rooms, three are lost or stolen, the one at Frostcrag was sold to a wizard who wanted it as a curiosity. A wizard! If the seal opens, it will not be a cloud-keep that answers. Fetch the Frostcrag bell and I will trust you with the rest.

frostcrag_spire.hook: A single obsidian spire on a rock in a cold sea, with no stairs: only a levitation or boat to the door and a storm-room at the top.
frostcrag_spire.rumour: The Spire sings in storm weather. Fishermen say it hums the same note as the old priory bell.

notes.title: A Wizard's Refusal
notes.author: Aldaril Fenmoore
pages: You ask me to give up the best bell I have ever heard, to men in grey who say a door will open. Doors have been opening in my head for forty years and I rather like the draught. Bring me a better note and we will talk.

sancre_tor.hook: A mountaintop Akaviri fortress above a barrow of dragon-hunters, with pagoda-curved halls over long tomb galleries.
sancre_tor.rumour: Sancre Tor's walls once rang. The hunters swore the barrow's gate rings three notes on the night before a storm.

notes.title: On the Vigils of Sancre Tor
notes.author: Hatsu the Archivist
pages: We came in boats from the east with orders to guard a door. The door was already guarded by the ones who built it. We stayed. We hung our bells to keep our dead company. When the empire forgot us, the bells became a lock. If you ring all seven, you will know what we are guarding. Do not.

notes.title: Archivist's Bone-Note
notes.author: Archivist Sevrin Dal
pages: Bone nineteen of forty-one: taken from the Sancre Tor barrow in the winter of last year. A Tsaesci in a monk's robe made the cut, courteous, and left a donation. I did not stop him; I did not know the count. Forty-one graves, forty-one bones. I do not know where the others are. I suspect the east.

imperial_bridge_inn.hook: An inn half on a stone bridge and half on the bank, with lanterns strung along the span and the river passing beneath its floorboards.
imperial_bridge_inn.rumour: The river under the Bridge Inn drops every year though it rains. The keeper pays a tax nobody can name.

notes.title: Water Tax, Bridge Inn
notes.author: Haldis Merrow
pages: Paid to the Ring: 22 gold, spring. 24, summer. 29, autumn. For the Bridge Inn's water rights, granted in a charter nobody has seen. I asked a clerk in Chorrol. She went white and said 'sluice 14'. I do not know what that means. The cellar wheel turns by itself some nights.

khuul.hook: A single street of ash-grey houses on a sea cliff with a long wooden stair running down to the water and a lantern at every landing.
khuul.rumour: In Khuul, someone walks the cliff stair asleep every night. The elders leave the lanterns lit and do not wake them.

notes.title: The Elder's Diary
notes.author: Selvil Sathram
pages: Eleven this winter. Nine walked up the stair in the night with their eyes shut and their lips moving. I asked the youngest what she was saying. She said, 'Counting steps.' A Temple pilgrim told me the ash is dreaming, not them. I told her to take her theology elsewhere. We keep lanterns lit. It is all we can do.

ald_velothi.hook: A harbour village of one temple and many boat-houses along a bay where the water goes grey from fallen ash.
ald_velothi.rumour: Ald Velothi hasn't put a boat out at night in months. They say the dreamers wade into the bay and stand there till dawn.

notes.title: Night-Watch Roster
notes.author: Priest Ilar Dren
pages: Watch rotates to the bay at dusk. DO NOT wake a standing sleeper. If one reaches the temple wall, tie a ribbon to the wrist; in the morning, count the ribbons. Last night: nineteen. We carried three back. Two of the three still ask which way is the mountain.

urshilaku_camp.hook: An Ashlander camp of yurts under hide, a wise woman's fire in the centre, and sleeping-mats ringed in ash-cord.
urshilaku_camp.rumour: The Urshilaku wise woman has been saying the ash is awake and has been for a year. The Temple laughs. The sleepers do not.

notes.title: Wise Woman's Fireside Prayer
notes.author: Sul-Matuul's heir
pages: Hold the knot, keep the flame, say each name, do not sleep. The ash has eyes this season. The fence is wearing thin and something stands at the doorway of it, patient as a stone. Ancestors, lend me your eyes, for I have kept them closed too long.

ghostfence_morrowind.hook: A long wall of shimmering ghost-light enclosing the mountain, broken at gate-posts and humming at a pitch just below hearing.
ghostfence_morrowind.rumour: The ghostfence has a gap you can see only at dusk, shaped like a person. It moves.

notes.title: Warden's Notice
notes.author: Ghostfence Warden
pages: THE FENCE HAS A WALKER. Do not go through at dusk, do not carry a lantern through, do not follow the sleepers. The breach is a mile from the gate-posts and growing. Every night a little closer to the crater. Report to the Temple at once. They have not answered the last six.

notes.title: Wind-Map Note
notes.author: Scholar Ranyl Telvani
pages: I have measured the fall for nine years. The ash falls where there are people with something to forget: a city of refugees, a mining colony, a village that fled. It is not random. It is drawn. If you wish to know what the volcano is saying, follow the wind and listen to what the ash does when it lands.

missamsi.hook: A corrupted ashland sanctum of blighted stone and red crystal growths, descending through ash-choked halls to a pulsing chamber.
missamsi.rumour: Something under Missamsi is still keeping a bed warm. Stay out of the ash after dusk.

notes.title: Cultist's Journal
notes.author: Neloth Ulven
pages: Eighth night. They come to us now unbidden and lie down in the ash as quietly as children. The Voice does not speak but the crystals hum in our teeth. It does not want worship, it wants us to stay. I think it is lonely. When I told the others, they laughed. I have started to dream of rooms with no doors.

kogoruhn.hook: A blasted ash-fortress at the foot of the mountain, with broken keeps half-buried in drifts and a collapsed amphitheatre.
kogoruhn.rumour: At Kogoruhn the ash seats are full of sleepers. They don't turn their heads when you walk through.

notes.title: The Audience
notes.author: a Kogoruhn sleeper
pages: ~We came in slippers and we came in silk,~we came by milk-road and by milk,~we sat in rows on a seat of ash,~the lights went down with a gentle crash.~Someone hums on the stage tonight:~it is not a song, it is only light.

seyda_neen.hook: A tiny customs-house port at a lagoon edge, with a silt-strider stop, a pier and a lighthouse with a ledger-room.
seyda_neen.rumour: The Seyda Neen clerk says there are more pilgrims coming in than going out. She has stopped opening the post.

notes.title: Customs Ledger, Pilgrims
notes.author: Clerk Edeth Brine
pages: Landed this month: 212. Departed: 41. Marked 'in transit': 171. In transit to where? The Temple says the canton, the canton says Mournhold, Mournhold says Seyda Neen. I stamp them and they walk inland. Not one has come back through my gate.

pelagiad.hook: A fortified hill village with a half-built fort and a granary where the roads from the pier all meet.
pelagiad.rumour: Every night the pilgrims leave the Pelagiad granary in a quiet line. The captain locks his door.

notes.title: Captain's Night Report
notes.author: Captain Ulric Dorn
pages: Pilgrims: 44 departed on the old road, 0 returned. Escort refused; the order was countersigned by the Temple's own seal. I would like it noted that I do not like this. The chalk crescents change colour after rain, and the line of travellers follows the new colour.

fields_of_kummu.hook: A green flat of old standing shrines in ash grass, each carved with a face that looks toward the lagoon.
fields_of_kummu.rumour: The Kummu shrines are tended by clerks nobody has met. They keep a ledger of tokens left and tokens never taken.

notes.title: Shrine Token Inventory
notes.author: Unsigned clerk
pages: Faces tended: 31. Tokens collected: 388. Tokens waiting: 1,904. Procedure: return tokens to the Sunken House at Ald Sotha, where the canton's keepers will file them. If a pilgrim asks for their token, tell them it is being kept safe. Do not tell them where.

ald_sotha.hook: A huge ancient Velothi shrine fortress with dusky green stone, great doors and a sunken lower temple of a long-silent god.
ald_sotha.rumour: Ald Sotha's lower rooms flood and drain on a schedule. Some say a clerk's bell rings down there.

notes.title: Lintel of the Filing Hall
pages: HERE THE WAITING ARE KEPT. Whoever comes in faith shall be remembered, whoever comes in doubt shall be counted. Take a token, leave a token. The quiet house does not close.

vivecs_antlers.hook: Two giant antlered peaks over the Stonefalls coast, one broken, with a pilgrims' ladder rungs worn smooth.
vivecs_antlers.rumour: The pilgrims' ladder on the broken antler goes up and the pilgrims go up and I have never seen one come down.

notes.title: Rung Inscription
pages: THE LADDER ENDS WHERE THE FAITHFUL DO. Take off your shoes at the bottom: you shall not need them. The quiet house welcomes all who climb with a quiet heart. Do not look down.

hla_oad.hook: A tidal fishing village of smoke-racks where the tide leaves mudflats scattered with brass glints.
hla_oad.rumour: The Hla Oad mudflats give up brass at every ebb. A trader pays triple if it has a little thumb-print.

notes.title: Brass Receipts
notes.author: Collector's agent
pages: Paid: 3 coin per thumbed cog, 1 coin per plain. Total this month: 214 thumbs. Deliver to the master at Balmora via Gnaar Mok. Do not clean them. The print is the point. No questions of the sea-folk; they have found more than we can carry.

gnaar_mok.hook: A muddy swamp town raised on stilts with a mangrove market and a landing for silt striders.
gnaar_mok.rumour: A stall in the Gnaar Mok market sells receipts and nothing else. Someone's always buying.

notes.title: Courier's Contract
notes.author: Mavos Hlaren
pages: I, the undersigned courier, agree to deliver parcels of brass to the Balmora cellar without opening them, listening to them, or answering when they speak. The master pays on delivery. The master will explain, in due time, what the guest requires.

notes.title: Strongbox Lid
pages: THE CRESCENT LEDGER KEEPS ITS DEBTORS. THE DEBTORS KEEP THEIR YEARS. If you open this box you will know each name on it, and each name owes you. Be a creditor or a liberator. The swamp does not tell you which is easier.

rkuldumz_spire.hook: A tall brass-pipe tower on a rock island off the Telvannis coast, whose top vents steam at fixed hours.
rkuldumz_spire.rumour: Rkuldumz steams once at the turn of every tide and the brass glints on the mud shift on the hour.

notes.title: Telvanni Surveyor's Notes
notes.author: Master-Surveyor Erilas
pages: The spire sounds a note I cannot hear but my mushroom-tower's tiles do. Each steam-peak, the cogs on the coast shift an inch toward Balmora, as if called. It is not a beacon; it is a summons. Something wants to be whole and has been asking politely for two thousand years.

notes.title: The Spire's Summit Plate
pages: ALL DIALS ANSWER HERE. When the eighth hand meets its mark the spire speaks, and all the halls of the world awaken at once. This may be a recall or a release. The dial does not distinguish. Hold the hand or let it fall. Choose carefully, hearer.

halls_of_fabrication.hook: A conveyor-and-forge hall with long assembly lines of half-built animunculi and a forge-pit finale, hammer sounds echoing in foundry glow.
halls_of_fabrication.rumour: Hammer-sounds in the Halls of Fabrication again. The machines are making something, but they never finish.

notes.title: Dwemer Line-Overseer's Slate
notes.author: an unknown Dwemer hand
pages: All lines run. All parts accounted for, save one: the Attendant's thumb. Without the thumb the Attendant cannot sign, and without the signature the Attendant cannot be released. Hold station until it returns. We will hold station.

arkngthand.hook: A Dwemer city-hall of cranking bronze with giant gear-halls, steam vents and a centrifuge chamber at the core.
arkngthand.rumour: Arkngthand still turns, one revolution an hour. Locals say there is someone in the middle of it, waiting.

notes.title: Centrifuge Plate
pages: ATTENDANT, SEAT UNTIL RETURN. The masters will come back by the third turn of the age. If they do not, the Attendant is released. If they do, the Attendant will answer for the delay.

notes.title: Tinkerer's Dial Notes
notes.author: Tinker Beldrar
pages: Dial two: Arkngthand, centrifuge side. Same figure as the first, same hand, same tick. I was told the dials were calibrated to local time. They are not. They are calibrated to each other. One hand moves, they all move. One dial stops, they all stop. This is a signal, not a clock.

tel_branora.hook: A single huge mushroom tower on a lagoon, with a master and his servants and a tidal causeway that floods twice a day.
tel_branora.rumour: The master of Tel Branora has been dead for six years. His letters still arrive every season.

notes.title: A Steward's Confession
notes.author: Steward Vanya
pages: My lord has not left the lower hall since the third flood. The papers still need signing, and each season the signature appears on its own, a little more crooked. I have stopped asking. The servants set his place and clear it. The vote requires his seat, they say; the seat is filled.

aldhaven_harbor.hook: A small harbour on the Iliac Bay's shore with a heavy chain across the mouth and a tidal slip for night barges.
aldhaven_harbor.rumour: A barge with no cargo but dust slips out of Aldhaven every ninth night and comes back lighter.

notes.title: Chain-Keeper's Log
notes.author: Hob Cranley
pages: Ninth night. Manifest: stone dust, chisels, one priest. Departed the chain at the ninth bell. Returned the third. No priest. No dust. Fresh-cut chips on the deck. I was paid to open the chain and asked to forget. I have not forgotten. The priest wore a Wayrest-sealed ring.

glenpoint.hook: A small walled port on a headland with a single gate, a beacon keep and houses crowded to the end of the quay.
glenpoint.rumour: The beacon at Glenpoint is lit on nights no ship is expected, and a grinding wheel runs in the boat-shed until dawn.

notes.title: Beacon-Keeper's Report
notes.author: Beacon-Keeper Orla
pages: Beacon lit nine nights this month on orders I did not give. A grinding wheel runs in the old boat-shed, and the quay is wet with stone dust at dawn. The barge that pauses there carries no flag. Its passengers are masons, and its cargo is wrapped in sacking. They pay me in good coin to look at the sea. I look at the sea.

cath_bedraud.hook: A knight's crypt under a ruined chapel with long vaulted aisles of effigies, a bone-lined crypt and a hollow font.
cath_bedraud.rumour: In Cath Bedraud the knights' stone faces all look one way: toward a niche that has been plastered shut.

notes.title: Effigy Plinth
pages: HE WHO WAS NOT COUNTED LIES HERE UNDER A BORROWED NAME. Seven he stood beside and an eighth he stood above. Let the chisel rest. Let the plaster crack. Let the heirs be found.

tomb_of_lost_kings.hook: A dynasty's necropolis with named sarcophagi and a family tree carved on the great wall, each room one king.
tomb_of_lost_kings.rumour: The Tomb of Lost Kings has an eighth door that some days is there and some days is not.

notes.title: The Seven (and One)
notes.author: the Archivist of the Tomb
pages: First: seated. Second: seated. Third: seated. Fourth: seated. Fifth: seated. Sixth: seated. Seventh: seated. Eighth: to be replastered under the seal of Wayrest, Daggerfall and Camlorn. The Eighth had two sons. Do not look for them.

the_lonely_lantern.hook: A one-lamp inn on a moor in the fog, with a single lantern in the window and a table laid for a guest.
the_lonely_lantern.rumour: The Lonely Lantern keeps its one lamp lit all night. Guests who sleep there leave a card and no footprints.

notes.title: A Card on the Table
pages: You are cordially invited to the supper that never ends. Wear what you wore when you were happiest. Leave your lantern at the door. The host is quite certain you will come. R.S.V.P. with the fog.

moiras_hope.hook: A tiny shrine hamlet on a moor-edge, with a single prayer-stone ringed in candle-ends and a bell that does not ring.
moiras_hope.rumour: At Moira's Hope the villagers light a candle for each who says yes to the fog.

notes.title: A Mourner's Prayer
notes.author: Wynne of Moira's Hope
pages: Lady of hope, hold my lantern. I said I would not go, and then I did, and then I could not tell you which way is back. If the fog sings tonight, do not let me answer. If the fog asks, let me remember I have a name.

northpoint.hook: A rock-bound northern port on a moor with houses clinging to a sea cliff, stairs down to the quay and a squat lighthouse in the mist.
northpoint.rumour: The lighthouse at Northpoint is dark at the fog hour, by order of the harbour-master, who wears a small silver bell round his neck.

notes.title: Harbour-Master's Orders
notes.author: Harbour-Master Dunstan
pages: Light to be extinguished at the fog hour. Ships to take their bearing by the moor-lanterns, not the great lamp. If a ship answers a voice from the fog, it is to be hailed back by the silver bell. If the ship does not respond, it is the Captain's affair and God keep him. Do not ask who is calling. The caller is polite.

doomcrag.hook: A black spire on a crag with spiral wards, a library of bound books and a roof with a storm engine.
doomcrag.rumour: The Doomcrag library has a ledger of names, and the necromancer reads it every night.

notes.title: A Bargain in Plum Ink
notes.author: Hestrel Doom
pages: I, Hestrel of the Crag, hereby supply to the Host of the Supper the register of the grieving of Rivenspire, with notes. In return I receive one tome of my choosing, and the Host's solemn word that I shall never be asked to attend. Signed, in my own best hand and a little fear.

sanguines_demesne.hook: A realm-pocket of red velvet with banqueting halls, endless mirror corridors and a throne of bones where the party has gone on too long.
sanguines_demesne.rumour: The invitations say the supper is held in a demesne of red velvet, where no one is unhappy and no one remembers the way home.

notes.title: Supper Song
notes.author: a guest
pages: ~The wine is red and the music high,~the candles never think to die.~We dance and eat and laugh and bow,~and none of us remember how~we came, or why, or when to leave.~The fog is thick. We do not grieve.

morkul_stronghold_high_rock.hook: A small Orc palisade in the Wrothgarian foothills with forges roaring and a hide-covered stone at its gate.
morkul_stronghold_high_rock.rumour: At Morkul they carve no name on the stone, and yet one appears each dusk. The smith won't speak of it.

notes.title: Smith's Warning
notes.author: Gro-Bramma
pages: Do not read the stone. If you read a name you know, say nothing. The date is nine days. If a name is yours, go to the Paragon's column before the date and ask who carved it. Do not tell your clan. They will try to stop it with spears.

paragons_remembrance.hook: A tall memorial column of names, with a flat processional ground before it and a bowl for offerings.
paragons_remembrance.rumour: The Paragon's column shows names of Orcs who are still alive, and they have started to die in that order.

notes.title: The Newest Names
notes.author: the mason
pages: Cut this season by no hand I know: Dura gro-Mazog, Grat Quick-Eye, Ushnar. Dura died on the date. Grat has seven days. Ushnar I do not know. I have tried covering the lower tier; the names grow up through the cloth. Someone is writing on the stone from the inside.

wrothgarian_mountains.hook: A broken ridge where the sky is a permanent dusk and sharp peaks throw shadows that never change.
wrothgarian_mountains.rumour: At noon the shadows on the Wrothgarian ridge fall the wrong way, and the sky there is the colour of permanent dusk.

notes.title: Cairn Warning
notes.author: a ridge-warden
pages: Do not look at the shadow's tip at noon. It is a line, and it points to a place, and the place is a hammer. The Orcs who looked have not slept well since. The line crosses the Chief's hall and ends in the old forge beneath the city. I have built a cairn on it in the hope it will think twice.

old_orsinium.hook: The first Orc city, buried, with huge sloping halls in blackened stone, tilted streets, a trophy-ringed throne and a collapsed forge.
old_orsinium.rumour: In Old Orsinium a hammer rings against an anvil with no smith, and it is carving something.

notes.title: The Anvil's Edge
pages: HE WHO HOLDS THE HAMMER KEEPS THE ACCOUNT. I do not choose, I only cut. If you would stop me, take the hammer, and be the one who cuts. Or break it, and let the names be what they are: unwritten, free.

notes.title: Anvil's Mark
pages: THE THIRD SMITH BROKE THE CROWN. The fourth smith broke the sword. The fifth smith did not break the ring, for she could not; she buried it in the forge, and the forge forgot. Let no hand lift it, for a ring lifted is a ring that remembers its finger.

koeglin_village.hook: A cliff-side village under a lighthouse on the Stormhaven coast, with steep stairs and nets hung from the cliff edge.
koeglin_village.rumour: The Koeglin nets are hauling up salt water from where there's no water to haul.

notes.title: Net-Mender's Notes
notes.author: Brenna of Koeglin
pages: Drip count, cup one: forty to the hour. Cup two, from the inn: sixty. The giant's cheek is wet at noon. I asked the old men. They said his tears are the sea and he has never stopped. I asked who is making him cry. Nobody knew. The water tastes of iron and hot copper.

weeping_giant.hook: An inn built under a toppled stone giant, whose cheek is wet at every hour and whose tears fall into a basin by the door.
weeping_giant.rumour: The giant over the Weeping Giant inn weeps salt. Folk say it is the sea trying to get out.

notes.title: The Innkeeper's Cup
notes.author: Maddoc Fell
pages: Day 112 of pouring. The tears do not stop. I collect them in a cup and pour the cup into the sea, and in the morning the cup is full again. The water tastes of rust and something sweeter. I asked a Direnni scholar. He did not laugh. He asked where the cellar drain leads.

notes.title: Innkeeper's Hush Diary
notes.author: Maddoc Fell
pages: The tears stopped last night. The first time in a hundred and thirteen days. I sat with the cup beneath the cheek and waited, and none came, and I wept myself. I do not know why I wept. There was a lullaby in the wind and I did not recognise the tongue. It was the gentlest thing I ever heard. I did not want it to stop.

isle_of_balfiera.hook: A hill-island with a ring of ruined towers in the bay, half-sunk at high tide.
isle_of_balfiera.rumour: The Isle of Balfiera is a few inches lower each year, though the tides are the same.

notes.title: Lock-Tower Survey
notes.author: Magistrate Anwen
pages: The ring of towers is a lock, not a fortification. Each tower guards a drain-sluice to the isle's underside. The island is sinking because the pump drinks from beneath it. If the pump is closed at the cliff-bastion, the isle will rise. I will submit this to the court. They will not read it.

mthartzel.hook: A Dwemer cliff-bastion with a bridge-and-gear gate and high steam halls above a drained cavern.
mthartzel.rumour: Mthartzel's steam rises on the hour, and every hour a little more water vanishes from the bay.

notes.title: Overseer's Pump Notes
notes.author: a Dwemer hand
pages: Pump One draws from the Lower Cavern at forty gallons a bell. The Direnni asked for a thing that could weep; we built it, and ran it dry. It must be fed. It must be fed. Do not close the valve while the giant still thirsts.

notes.title: Gauge-Wall Plate
pages: DIAL SIX. PRESSURE: NIL. TIME: UNTIL. The pump is no longer the first concern of this hall. The hall exists for the dial. If the dial reaches its mark, every pump will cease at once and every door will open. Let it reach its mark. Let us be recalled.

direnni_tower.hook: A tall white elven tower on an island, the old Direnni seat, with a spiral stair and a crystal lens at the summit.
direnni_tower.rumour: The old white tower of the Direnni stands on its island and a light burns in its lens-room every night. No one has been seen to climb the stair.

notes.title: A Letter Unsent
notes.author: Aralorne Direnni
pages: I made the giant to weep for her because I could not. She would have laughed. Now the sea comes through the giant's eyes and the isle sinks by an inch. I cannot stop it; I cannot bear the silence of a still cheek. Forgive an old man. Let the pump close when I am gone.

the_silver_pilgrim.hook: A roadhouse on the Dragontail road, a long low building with a well-yard and a tally-board hung from the eaves.
the_silver_pilgrim.rumour: The Silver Pilgrim's tally-board gets a new line every dawn, in a hand nobody knows.

notes.title: Tally-Board Copy
notes.author: Innkeeper Jabari
pages: Wells owed: thirty-one. Wells paid: nine. Caravans in arrears: forty-two. Collector: the Herald, who is not a man I have ever met. I copy the board each dawn and burn the copy. The board is always new again. It is a sort of mercy to be owed by someone who cannot be seen.

goats_head_oasis.hook: A well-oasis with palms and a half-buried statue of a goat, its horns visible above the sand.
goats_head_oasis.rumour: The Goat's Head well is an inch lower every season, and the goat statue is half-buried now.

notes.title: The Goat's Account
pages: Count nine paces from the left horn at dawn, dig under the shadow's tip. The first well was capped when the city's king drew the sand about his shoulders. Below it, a shaft. Below the shaft, a tithe. Bring water or bring no one.

volenfell.hook: A Dwemer ruin under a dune, half-flooded with sand, with mechanical halls and drifts.
volenfell.rumour: Volenfell hums when the wind is right. The old shepherds say it drinks.

notes.title: Pump Plate
pages: PUMP SEVEN: DRAWS FOR THE KING OF THE SAND. Do not stop while the king still lives. When the king is dead, continue until the king is remembered. Pump Seven shall not be stopped by the living.

notes.title: Digger's Dial Report
notes.author: Digger Hamza
pages: Found under a dune, a bronze plate with a hand that moves. I did not touch it. It ticked all night. At dawn a second hand appeared on the same dial, thin as a hair, and began to move faster. I do not like it. I have covered it with a goat-skin. I have asked a priest. He said it is not a prayer.

motalion_necropolis.hook: A tiered necropolis cut into a cliff, crowded with sarcophagus niches and a lightless stair.
motalion_necropolis.rumour: The necropolis at Motalion has a cold wind that blows out of the empty niche.

notes.title: The Heralds' Roll
notes.author: a tomb-scribe
pages: Eleven heralds are laid in niches. The twelfth niche stands open. The twelfth has not died but does not live. The twelfth carries the king's bell and rings it at each oasis at dawn. It is not to be spoken to. It will not answer, but it will remember.

tuwhaccas_throne.hook: A ceremonial throne-hall of an ancient king with a procession of statues, colossal doors and a long colonnade.
tuwhaccas_throne.rumour: At Tuwhacca's Throne the statues' heads all face a door. Some mornings one has moved.

notes.title: The King's Last Decree
pages: LET NO WELL RUN DRY WHILE I SLEEP. LET EVERY CARAVAN PAY. LET THE CITY OPEN ONLY WHEN THE LAST CUP IS RETURNED. This is the word of the sand, which is more patient than any king.

notes.title: Throne-Warden's Report
notes.author: Warden Qasim
pages: The east arm of the throne was cut away in the dry season by a thief who left the sword and the ring and took only this. The arm bore a name in a script I have not seen anywhere else. I copied it before the arm was taken. It reads: HOLLOW. I do not know what else. I am afraid to say it twice.

lost_city_of_the_na_totambu.hook: A buried city under the dunes, sand-choked streets below ground, a sunken temple and glass-roofed houses lit by a thin shaft of light.
lost_city_of_the_na_totambu.rumour: At noon the lost city lets a single beam through its glass roof, and the dunes above seem to breathe.

notes.title: Prayer to the Full Cup
notes.author: the dune-priests
pages: O Cup, O Well, O Water that waits. We give you back what we have drunk. Take the debt from the caravan and the debt from the child. Let the sand be sand again, and the king be a king in memory only. Let the cup be full.

valley_of_scars.hook: A canyon whose walls are carved with battle-reliefs from rim to floor, in a rust-red stone.
valley_of_scars.rumour: A fresh scene appears on the Valley of Scars each season. Guides now sell tours before it fills in.

notes.title: A Guide's Notes
notes.author: Samira the Guide
pages: The panels used to be old. Now they are new. A dozen figures on a stair, and one of them has a face I have seen in my tour-books. Each season another is carved. Nobody sees the chisel. I tell visitors it is only a trick of the light. It is not a trick of the light.

dragonstar.hook: A fortress-city with a huge circular arena at its heart, spokes of streets running to a ringed wall and a stepped palace beyond.
dragonstar.rumour: The arena-master of Dragonstar sets his bouts by a schedule he keeps in a locked chest, and the fighters who have read it won't discuss it.

notes.title: Arena-Master's Schedule
notes.author: Arena-Master Idris
pages: Bout one: a red-sash against a blue-sash, ending on the stair's third rung. Bout two: a drawn sword, a dropped shield, a kneeling. The valley's panels are filling at a rate of one bout a week. Fighters who refuse wake bruised in the shape of the bout they skipped. I do not make the fights. I merely schedule them.

aetherian_archive.hook: A giant sealed library sphere half out of the sand, its surface covered in turning glyph-rings.
aetherian_archive.rumour: The great sphere's rings turn at dusk, always to the same heading. Scholars come to watch and write nothing down.

notes.title: The Roll of Panels
notes.author: the archivist-sphere
pages: Panel the First: the climbers. Panel the Last: a stair to nowhere, and a figure who steps off it. The panels foretell the stair, not the fall. Whoever stands where the last panel stands will choose whether the stair is an ending or a door. The roll does not know.

sanctum_ophidia.hook: A serpent-cult sanctum of coiled-column rooms with spiral ramps, scale-patterned floors and a mirror-pool.
sanctum_ophidia.rumour: The serpent cult of Sanctum Ophidia coils its pool-mirror toward the stair and awaits an end to the world with perfect good manners.

notes.title: Serpent Cult's Evening Prayer
notes.author: the Ophidian cult
pages: Coil, coil, and coil once more. The stair is long and the mirror deep. We have seen what the panels foretell: a figure on a stair, a stepping off. We ask only to be swallowed gently when the Great Coil comes. We have swept the floors, polished the scales, and kept the pool quite clear. Come when you are ready.

skyreach_pinnacle.hook: A spire of rock standing alone in dunes, ringed by stairs that wind to a small platform at the top.
skyreach_pinnacle.rumour: The lone spire of Skyreach has a stair wound around it and a step-off notch at the top. The cult wants a figure to fall, and so does the arena.

notes.title: The Platform's Notch
pages: HERE THE LAST PANEL STANDS. A figure steps; a figure falls; a figure walks on. The stone does not say which. The valley's carving is a forecast, not a command. Stand where the panel stands and choose, and let the stone be surprised.

thrall_cove.hook: A slavers' former cove with rotting pens on a half-tide beach and a cliff stair of rusted rings.
thrall_cove.rumour: Thrall Cove's freedmen all have a palm-leaf pinned to their coat. They don't say what they plant.

notes.title: A Freedman's Contract
notes.author: Steward of Hubalajad
pages: The bearer, being free, agrees to plant and tend such palms as the lord shall provide, in such place as shall be named, for a period of twenty years. The bearer will be told the place when needed. The bearer will not be told why. Wages paid in water.

abahs_landing.hook: A pier-and-stilt harbour on a bay, with rope walkways, nets and a lighthouse on a mole.
abahs_landing.rumour: The stilt harbour at Abah's Landing ships palm-seeds in sealed jars. Nobody knows which garden they are for, and the harbour-master has stopped asking.

notes.title: Harbour-Master's Report
notes.author: Harbour-Master Nasir
pages: Jars of palm-seed received this season: 212, labelled 'for the garden', each stamped with a lord's palm-seal. Destination: overland, by night cart. I asked a cart-driver which garden. He said he only drove as far as the necropolis road and was paid not to look. I have kept the manifests in a locked drawer.

hubalajad_palace.hook: A walled lord's estate in the Hews Bane hills, with a long colonnade and a conservatory of potted palms.
hubalajad_palace.rumour: At Hubalajad the lord has been dead twenty years and still orders palms by the barrow-load.

notes.title: Steward's Palm Ledger
notes.author: the Steward
pages: Planted this season: 31. Rooted: 28. Blooming: 4. The lord's line is long; the garden is long; the list is long. I do not ask what blooms. I record the water. The bloom is said to cure the sand-fever, but only in blood of the line. I am no physician.

ahaleb_necropolis.hook: A mid-size necropolis with a long bridge hall over a pit, a hidden oasis chamber of palms under skylights and a final stair of golden doors.
ahaleb_necropolis.rumour: Ahaleb has a garden underneath that glows green at noon, if you stand on the right dune.

notes.title: A Gardener's Diary
notes.author: Hadiya
pages: I do not remember coming. I remember a contract, a palm, and a glass of water. I tend. The dead are warm. The bloom is gold and very beautiful, and when I touch it I feel my name loosening. I think this is how the gardens keep their gardeners. I must remember my name. Hadiya. Hadiya. Hadiya.

port_hunding.hook: A small port gate and pier on Stros M'Kai's coast, a customs hut and a harbour crane, with a sealed manifest cabinet.
port_hunding.rumour: Every fifth year a ship leaves Port Hunding with sealed cargo and the clerks are told to stay home.

notes.title: Customs Note
notes.author: Clerk Rahim
pages: Fifth year: one ship, sealed, no passengers declared. Crew: twelve, all of the old families. Destination: unrecorded. Return: not expected. I was ordered to accept the form without reading the cargo. I read it. I will not say what I read, except that the ship is old.

notes.title: Harbour Page Note
notes.author: Navigator Idris
pages: Page two of nine: hidden in the manifest cabinet at Port Hunding. It gives a tide-hour and a heading for the first stage. Hide it again. Do not carry it on the sea unless you have the others; a single page leads to a reef.

saintsport.hook: A shrine harbour on the Stros M'Kai coast, with a shrine to a drowned saint and a bell that rings under water.
saintsport.rumour: Saintsport's bell rings under water every fifth year, and a family goes quiet.

notes.title: Sailors' Prayer
notes.author: Saintsport shrine
pages: Saint of the swallowed bell, whom the sea took on the fifth year: hold the ship's tilt in your two hands. Bring us back or let us be the ones who did not come. We do not ask what we carry. We carry it. Amen. Amen. Amen.

draggin_tale_inn.hook: An inn with a giant draconian tail over the door, a long common room and a back room where the families meet.
draggin_tale_inn.rumour: The Draggin Tale's back room is shut every fifth spring while twelve families draw lots.

notes.title: The Twelve Families
notes.author: Innkeeper Baraka
pages: Aman, Bahrad, Cassim, Dalila, Emre, Farouk, Ghassan, Hadiya, Idris, Jabari, Karim, Layla. Each has sent a child on the fifth-year ship at least once. The lots are carved prows. This year's prow is white. I have drawn it for sixty years and never drawn mine.

onsis_breath.hook: A ring of wind-carved arches on the Bangkorai coast, whose stones sing in the wind with a hollow note.
onsis_breath.rumour: Onsi's arches hum on a westerly. The sailors say the wind is reading tides aloud.

notes.title: The Arch's Footing
pages: FIFTH YEAR: BRING THE PAGE. FIFTH YEAR: LEAVE THE PAGE. The ledger is torn in nine for the safety of the sea. One piece sleeps beneath this arch, until a captain who can read it comes.

notes.title: Wind-Bone Note
notes.author: Surveyor Hamid
pages: Onsi's arches are dragon vertebrae. One is replaced by a pale stone, cut to fit, with a tag: 'Number 23.' Beneath the stone is a dry niche where the true bone was. Whoever took it left a good copy and a note of thanks. I would have preferred an apology. The wind sings through the gap in the wrong key.

star_haven_adeptorium.hook: A tiny academy under a dome on an Anequina hillside, with a roof opening and brass quadrants on every windowsill.
star_haven_adeptorium.rumour: The Star Haven mage says Secunda is late and gets laughed at. He keeps measuring anyway.

notes.title: Observation Log
notes.author: Brother Za'ren
pages: Secunda late by seven minutes on the twelfth. Eleven on the fourteenth. The almanac of the priests declares the moon on time. I wrote respectfully, three times. The third answer asked me to stop looking up. I have bought a larger quadrant. The moon is not wrong. The moon is moving.

shrine_of_the_cats_divine.hook: A stepped shrine of giant cat statues on an Anequina hillside, with a moon-pool and a stair of prayer tablets.
shrine_of_the_cats_divine.rumour: The great cats at the shrine have started casting shadows that don't match the day.

notes.title: Pilgrim's Warning
notes.author: a pilgrim
pages: Do not light the evening lamp by the pool. The priests have changed the marks and the cats do not like it. A mason told me the new mark is wrong by a finger's breadth, and that a finger's breadth of moon is a month's grain. Say nothing to the priests. They will say it is blasphemy.

temple_of_agamanus.hook: A ridge-top temple with terraces in four stages, prayer-wheels and a hollow dome, whose sanctum is aligned to a single moonrise.
temple_of_agamanus.rumour: The temple of Agamanus no longer lights its lamp. The keepers say it will be lit again once the moon is on time.

notes.title: Keeper's Standing Orders
notes.author: High Keeper
pages: The lamp is not to be lit until the moon touches the dome. If it is late, it is late; do not alter the dome or the brass. Do not post this order. Do not tell the pilgrims. The moon is the moon, and it is the priests' duty to be right even when the moon is wrong.

tomb_of_the_moon_singers.hook: A choir-tomb of echoing chambers, each room tuned to a note of the moon's phase, cut into an Anequina hill.
tomb_of_the_moon_singers.rumour: The Moon Singers' tomb hums a note lower than it did when my mother was a kitten.

notes.title: The Choir-Mistress's Song
notes.author: Mistress Sa'ira
pages: ~Low is the moon and the note is low,~low is the song where the singers go.~Three keys for the gates, and a choir for each,~and the vault to the blades is a thing out of reach.~Sing it true, sing it true, sing it true,~till the moon rises up and is late no more.

vault_of_the_heavenly_scourge.hook: A sealed vault of lunar weapons, a long hall of racked blades that wake when moonlight enters the skylights and an antechamber of three keyed moon-gates.
vault_of_the_heavenly_scourge.rumour: The vault's blades hum at moonrise. Folk say they have started to hum before the moon comes.

notes.title: The Gate-Lintel
pages: THREE KEYS, THREE NOTES, THREE MOONRISES. Do not enter before the moon. Do not enter after. The blades wake to the moon that is, not the moon that was. If the moon is late, the blades are hungry.

roadside_twin_moons.hook: A roadhouse with two lanterns by the Rimmen road, one pale and one rose, each the colour of a moon.
roadside_twin_moons.rumour: A faceless Khajiit walked past the Twin Moons last night and bowed to the lanterns.

notes.title: Lanternkeeper's Letter
notes.author: Mazri
pages: To the Rimmen guard: I found a mask in the pack of a Baandari trader. It was one of the honoured dead's, with the family seal inside the rim. A faceless one came to the door later that night and stood in the road with its hands out. I did not give it anything. I am ashamed. Please send someone.

baandari_caravan_stop.hook: A tent camp by the Rimmen road with painted wagons, cooking fires and a bright awning for the trade.
baandari_caravan_stop.rumour: The Baandari tent camp by the Rimmen road will sell you anything, and lately that includes carved faces nobody asks about.

notes.title: Caravan-Mother's Account Book
notes.author: Caravan-Mother Rasha
pages: Faces bought this season: 38 (cedar), 21 (bone), 4 (gilt). Faces sold north: 51. Faces unsold: 12, kept in the wagon with the red awning. I had thought them craft-work. A priest told me otherwise and left in tears. I will sell no more. I cannot afford to stop.

notes.title: Caravan-Mother's Slips
notes.author: Caravan-Mother Rasha
pages: Caravans in debt: forty-six. Debts held by the Crescent Ledger: forty-one. We have always paid the Counting-House with a cut of the sugar and a season's labour of the young. Nobody has seen the lender. Nobody wishes to. It is said he sleeps by day and by night and pays his debts in years.

hakoshae.hook: A hamlet around a ring of upright moonstones where tomb-guardians live, low houses in the circle's shadow.
hakoshae.rumour: The Hakoshae guardians keep faceless dead in the ring at night. Don't walk near after dark.

notes.title: A Guardian's Diary
notes.author: Guardian Mur'ti
pages: Three more came last night. I counted them into the ring and gave them each a lamp. They stand and wait, and the moon looks down on their smooth faces. I have written to the priests of Rimmen four times. The fifth I shall carry myself. I am afraid of what I shall say.

anequina_aqueduct.hook: A long arched aqueduct across a gorge, with a channel on top and maintenance galleries running through its piers.
anequina_aqueduct.rumour: The aqueduct's piers are hollow, and on moonless nights lamps burn inside them.

notes.title: Smugglers' Packing List
notes.author: unsigned
pages: Box 1: eighteen masks, cedar. Box 2: eleven masks, bone. Box 3: the family seal-mask of House Rukhal, which is not for sale and I will not carry it. Box 4: empty, return with ballast. Water in the channel is low this season; take the lower gallery.

notes.title: Aqueduct-Keeper's Report
notes.author: Keeper Hakim
pages: The channel went quiet at the second bell. Not dry: quiet. The water stood still in its bed and a note came from the stones, a lullaby, a hum that I felt in my teeth. I tried to cry out and found I could not. At dawn I was lying in the channel with my cheek on the wet stone, and my face was wet with tears.

rimmen_necropolis.hook: A vast city of the dead in layers, with crypt avenues, moon-lit atria and a lunar clock chamber that descends with the moons' cycle.
rimmen_necropolis.rumour: The Rimmen necropolis has a clock that stopped between two moons. Some say it is waiting for faces.

notes.title: Clock-Chamber Epigraph
pages: EACH NICHE A FACE, EACH FACE A NAME. The clock does not run while a niche stands empty. It is not cruelty; it is order. Return what was taken. The dead are not impatient. They have time.

tathara_sugar_farm.hook: A sugar farm with a boil-house at the edge of a meadow where the cane is lit with a faint, moon-coloured glow.
tathara_sugar_farm.rumour: The Tathara sugar is brighter than any harvest. It tastes of iron, and the wife sleeps three days.

notes.title: Farmer's Notes
notes.author: Rashid of Tathara
pages: Sugar sold: two hundred weight. Sugar returned by customers: sixty. Complaints: the sleeping, the taste, the glow. The glow is worse by the meadow's lower ditch. I put my hand in the ditch and it came out shining. I have washed it twice. It is still shining.

moon_sugar_meadow.hook: A field of luminous moon-sugar flowers in a shallow bowl of pale earth, brightest along a drainage ditch.
moon_sugar_meadow.rumour: The meadow glows brightest along the ditch, and the ditch never freezes.

notes.title: Surveyor's Report
notes.author: Hasani
pages: The ditch leads under the hill, into a gallery of brass. The stone is warm. The glowing liquid is oil, not water, and it ticks as it cools. The farmers call it the moon's milk. I would call it a leak. I would also call for a very long rope.

notes.title: A Debt-Slip
notes.author: the Counting-House
pages: The bearer of this slip owes, to the Counting-House of the Crescent Ledger, thirty-one years of labour at the rate of one year per hundred weight of sugar. The debt is purchased from the farm of Tathara and transferred without notice. The bearer will continue to be paid in the farm's own coin, minus interest.

the_prancing_netch.hook: An inn built beneath a hanging netch-balloon on the Anequina road, with a long common room and a rooftop landing for ropes.
the_prancing_netch.rumour: The Prancing Netch's beer glows faintly on Fridays and nobody will say why.

notes.title: Cellar Ledger
notes.author: Innkeeper Tabu
pages: Kegs: 40. Tank: one, full, glowing. Complaints: three drinkers who slept for a day. Praise: sixteen drinkers who say it is the best they ever had. I have stopped serving it to the old and the very young. I have not stopped serving it. Do not tell the Senchal buyers.

corinthe.hook: A green river city of terraced gardens, canals with arching bridges and a garden-roofed cathedral.
corinthe.rumour: The cathedral of Corinthe has a ward of sleepers laid out like a field of sheaves, and the herbalists say the cure costs more than the town has.

notes.title: Herbalists' Ward Report
notes.author: Herbalist Mireth
pages: Sleepers in the nave: 63. Waking after a dose of river-moss: 41. Waking cleanly: 22. The moss grows only in the third canal and costs us a week's labour per dose. The cause is a glow in the sugar. The sugar-port buyers know it. We have written to them politely, then less politely. Please send moss.

halls_of_colossus.hook: A Dwemer hall of colossal machines with too-large doors and a giant half-assembled construct whose chest is cracked.
halls_of_colossus.rumour: The Halls of Colossus drip at night. The sugar-folk say the meadow grows from its tears.

notes.title: Colossus Plate
pages: UNFINISHED. DO NOT DRAIN. The cold-water must not touch the meadow-soil, for the soil is the colossus's keeper. Close the chest. Do not wake the chest. Do not wake the colossus.

notes.title: Colossus Dial Note
notes.author: Tinker Beldrar
pages: The seventh dial is under the great machine's ribs. It has turned three-quarters. It is the nearest to its mark of any I have seen. The colossus is a clock-weight for it. Whatever will come, it will come when the dial and the colossus agree. I have left the dial alone, and I have left the colossus alone, and I have left.

orcrest.hook: A mesa-top fort-town in orange rock, with a gate shaped like a pair of claws, cisterns and rooftop banners.
orcrest.rumour: Every caravan out of Orcrest carries one broken blade-shard. Nobody knows who sends them.

notes.title: Gate-Captain's Orders
notes.author: Captain Ja'dar
pages: One shard per caravan, ribbon tied, delivered to the hill. If asked, say it is custom. If asked again, say it is old. If asked a third time, hand over the ledger of oaths and let the questioner choose whether to carry the weight.

dune.hook: A caravan crossroads with a wheel-shaped market, eight radial lanes, striped tents and camel pens at the rim.
dune.rumour: The caravan market at Dune has a wagon at its hub that sells nothing and is never left unguarded.

notes.title: Hub-Wagon Ledger
notes.author: Wagon-Keeper Zhasira
pages: Shards received: 31. Shards forwarded to the plateau city: 24. Shards held back for the final carry: 7. I am told they are an old custom. I am told many things. The shards are warm in my hands at dusk, and they rattle in the night as though trying to arrange themselves. I keep them wrapped in wool and I do not look at them.

ne_quin_al.hook: An ancient ruined city on a plateau, with a processional road, collapsed towers and a single standing arch.
ne_quin_al.rumour: At Ne Quin-al the old smiths' oath-hall has a floor that someone has been tallying by hand, and the smith's anvil is warm to the touch.

notes.title: The Floor Tally
pages: NINE HUNDRED COLUMNS OF OATHS, NINE HUNDRED NAMES IN EACH. Each who swore on a blade is counted here, and each who broke it is counted twice. The blade that was shattered is not lost. It is borne to the hill. Whoever carries it must have broken a vow, and kept another. Such is the order of the forge.

hill_of_shattered_swords.hook: A hill planted with thousands of broken sword-blades, shining in the wind like a cold field of wheat.
hill_of_shattered_swords.rumour: The shards on the hill move at night. By morning they are in a ring, and there is always a gap.

notes.title: Song of the Hundred Oaths
notes.author: unknown
pages: ~A hundred oaths on a hundred steel,~a hundred hands that learned to kneel.~Bring the broken, bring the bent,~bring the oath that was never spent.~The hill is cold and the wind is long.~Come and be forged in the dragon's song.

prowls_edge_dragonscour.hook: A ridge of colossal bones leading to a lair on a mesa, an open-air scour you can walk inside with ribs forming arches.
prowls_edge_dragonscour.rumour: At Prowl's Edge a steam rises from the bones on a cold night, as if something were quenched.

notes.title: The Quench-Trough Rim
pages: WHAT IS SWORN IS SWORN. WHAT IS BROKEN IS BROKEN. WHAT IS FORGED HERE IS BOTH. Let no hand take the blade who has not broken a vow. Let no hand put it down who has not kept one.

elden_tree.hook: The great tree seen from the whole province, a trunk wide as a hill with a faintly glowing crown above the clouds.
elden_tree.rumour: The great tree's glow is a shade dimmer than last year. The keepers say it will be fine. The keepers are not looking up.

notes.title: Keeper's Warning
notes.author: Keeper Alduin Ro
pages: Do not touch the splinters. They are for the keepers' use only. Do not ask what they are for. If the crown goes dark we shall have the Ayleid dead to deal with, and I do not think the Green Pact has the words for it. Feed the lamp. Feed it names. We have run out of ours.

ne_salas.hook: A tower-city underground, a spiral of ring galleries around a central crystal pillar, bright and cold.
ne_salas.rumour: Under the great tree is a second light, say the root-diggers, one that doesn't flicker.

notes.title: The Pillar's Dedication
pages: WHAT WE NAME, WE KEEP. WHAT WE KEEP, WE LIGHT. Each lamp burns a name and each name must be renewed. Let no keeper forget this, nor the one who tends the crown: a lamp unfed becomes a door.

notes.title: Pillar Report
notes.author: Lampwright Ilvaren
pages: Ne Salas: the pillar relit at the fourth bell. A tone rose from it that no instrument could name. The cabal agrees that the stones are one voice and that we have only the third note of nine. We go to the Reliquary, then to the ashes. Say nothing to the Order.

reliquary_of_stars.hook: A domed observatory-vault whose ceiling is a map of the night sky in inlaid crystal, with floor rings that rotate by lever.
reliquary_of_stars.rumour: Under the reliquary's dome the stars go out one by one. The cartographers swear it was full of them a decade ago.

notes.title: The Keeper's Manual of Stars
notes.author: a lamp-warden
pages: The star-lamp is lit by names, the sky by lamps. Each star is a name; each name a debt. When the debt is paid the star may rest. When the debt is unpaid the star must be fed. The Keepers have forgotten how to feed them. The Reliquary remembers. It will not forgive.

notes.title: Star-Vault Tally
notes.author: Lampwright Ilvaren
pages: The ceiling is a chart, not a sky. Four stars lit, thirty to go, and the vault answers with niches opening. We read one scroll: it was a list of the lamps themselves, nine in all, ending at a place called the Tower of Ten Thousand Years. I think we have been told where to go.

ossuary_of_telacar.hook: A bone-walled ossuary built in terraced galleries, skulls arranged by family line, each tier's door answering to a name read aloud.
ossuary_of_telacar.rumour: The Ossuary doors will open if you read the right name aloud. Nobody remembers the right name.

notes.title: Lineage Plaque
notes.author: the ossuary's founders
pages: First tier: the Keepers. Second: the Lamp-Wardens. Third: the Name-Singers. Fourth: those who were not named. Fifth, flooded: the Warden whose name was struck. Speak it, and the lamp will know its keeper. Fail to speak it, and the lamp will not be fooled.

roadside_green_bough.hook: An inn in a boughed tree on the Malabal Tor road, with stair-ladders and a landing of woven rope.
roadside_green_bough.rumour: The walking city has been going in a straight line since spring. The innkeeper drew it on the wall.

notes.title: Route-Board Notes
notes.author: Innkeeper Nila
pages: The city's usual circle: spring in the north, summer to the east, autumn south, winter west. This year it has not circled. It goes straight, as though led. A hermit at Supplication House has a better map. She cut one of the guide-trees. Please do not tell the wardens.

supplication_house.hook: A hermit's hut deep in Malabal Tor with a prayer-bench, a wind-chime of bone and a ring of stumps around it.
supplication_house.rumour: The hermit at Supplication House is cutting trees and weeping while she does it. The wardens pretend not to hear.

notes.title: A Hermit's Confession
notes.author: Wynlith of the Stumps
pages: I have cut nine. The Pact says one cut is a death-sentence for the cutter, and I have cut nine, and still I breathe. The apostates' chant goes on. They call the great walker to them and I cannot bear what it will do. I have asked the Orcs. Orcs do not hold with the Pact. Orcs have axes.

drabul.hook: An Orc outpost in the Malabal forest, a palisade of cut trunks and a forge-pit beneath a canopy hole.
drabul.rumour: The Orcs of Drabul have been felling trees that Bosmer would not touch, and no Bosmer has said a word against them.

notes.title: Chief's Stump Tally
notes.author: Chief Gruzbash
pages: Guide-trees felled: 7. Remaining on our line: 4. Paid: smoked fish, two casks of ale, and a hermit's gratitude, which is the best I have been paid in. The hermit weeps when she hands over the axes. I do not understand her people's gods. I understand a good axe and a woman who needs a tree cut.

jathsogur.hook: An Orc stronghold on a ridge above the forest, with a stone keep and a view of the guide-tree line.
jathsogur.rumour: From Jathsogur's wall you can see the city's route. The Orcs have been shooting at the trees along it.

notes.title: Chieftain's Orders
notes.author: Chief Mazgar
pages: Eleven guide-trees remain on the line. Fell nine with the ballista, two by axe at dusk. Do not shoot at the city itself. Do not shoot at the Pact-wardens. If asked, we are hunting boar. Our payment is in smoked fish and the hermit's gratitude. It will have to do.

silvenar.hook: A hidden court under hollowed root arches, a sheltered amphitheatre of roots with a single audience hall lit by fireflies.
silvenar.rumour: The hidden court at Silvenar knows who is cutting guide-trees, and a councillor passes the cutters coin in secret.

notes.title: Councillor's Secret Letter
notes.author: Councillor Aerin
pages: To the hermit: the court cannot approve and will not forbid. A purse is enclosed, and a seal that will open the walking city's inner stairs. The chant of the apostates is a poison to the Pact and a danger to the city. Cut the last guide-trees at night. Do not be found. If you are found, we have never met.

tomb_of_the_apostates.hook: A hollow great tree whose heartwood is carved with tombs, stairs spiralling inside the trunk.
tomb_of_the_apostates.rumour: At dusk the hollow tree sings. The Pact-wardens put their hands over their ears and call it wind.

notes.title: Apostate's Chant
notes.author: the apostates
pages: Walk to us, great walker, tree of ten thousand roots. Walk to us who have been forgotten by the Pact. We offer the hollow, we offer the dark, we offer the quiet that is not a death. Walk and be ours. Walk and be still.

notes.title: A Pact-Warden's Notes
notes.author: Pact-Warden Lirael
pages: One panel gone from the heartwood: a carving of a crowned figure with its face hollowed out. The tree is not a tomb for the Pact's dead; it was a tomb for something older, planted over it to keep it quiet. The apostates' chant, I now suspect, was never to the great walker. It was to the thing in the heartwood.

marbruk.hook: A fort-town in a glade ringed by a living wall of thorn and stone, with a central fire pit and watch posts.
marbruk.rumour: The thorn wall of Marbruk has names pricked into it. The watchers bow every dusk and nobody asks why.

notes.title: The Thorn Plaque
pages: THESE ARE THE MERCIED. NEVER CUT. NEVER MOVED. We spared them from the fire and the sword, and they are green now, and they are ours, and they may not go home. Forgive us, keepers who come after: this is the cost of mercy.

labyrinth.hook: A hedge-and-root maze that rearranges each time you leave a junction, with carved arrows that lie and wisp-lights as false guides.
labyrinth.rumour: The Labyrinth hedge changes each time you look away. From the ridge you can see it is a map.

notes.title: Maze-Walker's Map
notes.author: Elorin the Wanderer
pages: From the ridge, the hedge is a street grid. The central cross is the market, the north lobes the lamp-wards. I have walked it three times and left a ribbon at each turning. The ribbons were gone by morning. The exit is at the old gate, and the gate is a thing you must be invited through.

city_of_ash.hook: A burned Ayleid city with ash-choked terraces, melted crystal lamps and a scorched grand cistern.
city_of_ash.rumour: The City of Ash is quiet. The ash holds the shape of people who sat down and did not get up.

notes.title: Elegy for the Lamps
notes.author: unknown
pages: ~Our lords put out the lamps and wept,~and wept, and fed the fire.~The trees took us, the trees have kept~the ash of our desire.~We lean, we lean, we lean for home,~for stone that has no tire.

notes.title: Ashes and Lamplight
notes.author: Lampwright Ilvaren
pages: The City of Ash was the worst. I lit the lamp and every ash-figure on the terraces turned its head. One said a word. I have not repeated it since. The cabal's youngest has gone pale. We have one stone left and a Tower to face. I would give a great deal for a quieter instrument to play.

waterdancer_falls.hook: A tall waterfall in Reaper's March with a spray rainbow and a prayer-stone at its base cut with eight notches.
waterdancer_falls.rumour: The prayer-stone at Waterdancer has eight notches and only seven bones. Both peoples avoid talking about the eighth.

notes.title: Falls Prayer
notes.author: Falls-priest
pages: Water that falls and does not break, hold the Truce for the two peoples. The bones are laid, the bones are white. If one is missing, let the water speak. If one is missing, let the water rise. We have not been honest with the water, and the water is patient, and the water remembers.

notes.title: Falls-Priest's Warning
notes.author: Falls-priest
pages: Do not stand at the base at midnight. The water stops, and you will hear a woman singing a lullaby in the old tongue. It is very gentle. It is not for you. Every fall is a verse and every verse a drowsier one. I do not know who she is singing to. I know that I will not be here when it is finished.

sren_ja.hook: A tree village of Khajiit in Reaper's March, with rope-bridges between boughs and drums at every platform.
sren_ja.rumour: At Sren Ja the drums stop at the eighth beat. The elders say it is for the dead drummer.

notes.title: The Seven Verses
notes.author: Sren Ja drummer
pages: ~One for the bough and two for the root,~three for the river and four for the fruit,~five for the sun and six for the moon,~seven for the rain and eight for the...~the drum is still and the verse is gone.~Whoever finds it, carry it on.

dokrin_monastery.hook: A forest monastery of the Khajiit with a courtyard of prayer-wheels and a small library of drum-scores.
dokrin_monastery.rumour: The monks at Dokrin keep the oldest drum-scores in the March. One page has been replaced with a pressed leaf, and the abbot weeps when anyone asks.

notes.title: Abbot's Library Notes
notes.author: Abbot Rasi
pages: Score nine, the Truce-song: eight verses, of which the eighth has been cut out and a leaf pressed in its place. The cutter left no mark but a clay thumb. I replaced the leaf nine times and nine times it was removed. I now keep it where it is. Whoever wants the verse may bring me the hand that holds it.

rawlkha.hook: A Khajiiti trade-town of canvas and bamboo stalls strung between trees, a lantern forest.
rawlkha.rumour: Rawlkha's lantern-market sells paper from a dozen stalls, and a verse that was stolen from a monastery has passed through eleven hands there.

notes.title: Paper-Seller's Ledger
notes.author: Paper-Seller Mizra
pages: Sold: one verse-leaf, pressed, from a monastery library. Buyer: a Bosmer in a scholar's coat. Previous buyers: ten. Glosses in the margin: eleven, in eleven hands. Each says something different about whose it was. I sold it for three coin and was glad. I was told afterward what it was, and have been unwell since.

thizzrini_arena.hook: A ruined arena in the jungle with a sand floor and tiers of stone seats half-eaten by roots.
thizzrini_arena.rumour: In the old arena a single footprint stays in the sand. No rain washes it out.

notes.title: Arena Keeper's Report
notes.author: Keeper Zhasi
pages: The footprint is neither Bosmer nor Khajiit. It has five toes and a heel. It sits in the exact centre of the sand and has been there for ten years. If you dance, you must step around it, as though around a sleeping animal. The eighth step is to step into it.

reapers_henge.hook: A stone circle with a bone-white altar on a rise in Reaper's March, ringed by eight standing stones.
reapers_henge.rumour: At the henge the altar is bright with bone. One seat has been empty for ten years.

notes.title: The Altar's Edge
pages: EIGHT BONES FOR THE EIGHT WINDS, ONE FOR EACH WHO WALKS HERE. The eighth is given by a stranger to both. It is not a bone of blood but a bone of choice. Lay it down, and the Truce is renewed. Hold it, and the Truce is broken.

isle_of_contemplation.hook: A tiny isle off Auridon with a single meditation platform, a sundial and a boat-landing of white stone.
isle_of_contemplation.rumour: The hermit on the Isle of Contemplation counts twenty-three bells every dusk and swears there should be twenty-four.

notes.title: Hermit's Bell-Tally
notes.author: Eldrael the Counting
pages: Dusk, day 21,918. Twenty-three bells. Dusk, day 21,919. Twenty-three. I asked the sun and the sun looked away. I asked the Order and was sent a kindly letter. I have filed the gnomon down so I will not be taunted by a shadow that has nowhere to fall. The missing hour is a place; I can feel it like a missing tooth.

colosseum_of_the_old_ways.hook: A ruined ring arena on Artaeum's shore, its floor a pale mosaic of hours and its tiers half-sunk in sand.
colosseum_of_the_old_ways.rumour: The Old Ways arena's floor has a grey tile where an hour should be. Nobody remembers the fight that was held there.

notes.title: Floor Inscription
pages: TWENTY-FOUR TILES FOR TWENTY-FOUR HOURS. LET NO HOUR BE PRIED. The tile that was lifted lies not here but where the hours are kept. A fight is held in every hour, and one was held in this, and one man lost it. His name is not the one on the pedestal.

traitors_vault.hook: A vault of false doors on Artaeum where each room offers three exits, two of which loop back through mirrors.
traitors_vault.rumour: The Traitor's Vault has more doors than rooms. The ones that open lead to the same place.

notes.title: Vault-Builder's Notes
notes.author: Architect Ilwen
pages: A hundred false doors, one real. The real one is the wall. Do not break it with a sword; use a hammer that remembers. The reward behind it is not gold but a thing the Order wished to forget, and they have paid me well for forgetting. I have forgotten. I am frightened at how easily.

crystal_tower_summerset.hook: A needle of crystal many times taller than anything, glowing at night, with a spiral of lens-rooms at its summit.
crystal_tower_summerset.rumour: The Crystal Tower's summit lenses were covered with a cloth at the spring equinox. The wardens won't say what they saw before they did it.

notes.title: Warden's Lens-Room Log
notes.author: Warden Aelwyn
pages: The first lens shows the sky as it is. The second shows the sky as it was a hundred years ago. The third shows a night with stars I cannot name and a door in the sky. I have covered the third with a cloth and set a guard, and told no one why. It is not my place to say. It is not my place to look.

notes.title: Magister's Orders
notes.author: the Lampwright Magister
pages: The ninth stone is the Tower's lens. When it is lit, the sky will show as it was. Be ready. The Ayleid names in the vaults below will rise, and the Psijic wardens will not be pleased. Do not let anyone near the lens-lever. It is not a thing that can be taken back.

psijic_relic_vaults.hook: A vault of sliding walls and phase-doors where rooms rearrange as you move and time-eddies freeze torches.
psijic_relic_vaults.rumour: The Psijic vaults move their rooms. Folk say there is one that has been moved so often it is no longer anywhere.

notes.title: The Candle's Plate
pages: THE HOUR IS KEPT, NOT KILLED. Let it burn until the one who spilled the cup is known. Let it not be hidden from the one who lost it. The Order has been wrong before; the Order will be wrong again. Let the hour be remembered.

notes.title: The Ninth Lamp
pages: THE NINTH LAMP BURNS NOT FOR LIGHT BUT FOR REMEMBRANCE. Those who tend it tend the dead. Those who extinguish it forget the dead. Those who keep it must be willing to hear, in the dark, all that was done in the light.

dawnbreak.hook: A hamlet on an Auridon bluff above the sea, with white cottages and a row of weathered crosses of crystal.
dawnbreak.rumour: At Dawnbreak a man walked into the sea last winter. His eyes shone like cut glass the week before.

notes.title: A Widow's Diary
notes.author: Tilwen of Dawnbreak
pages: He began to see the stars at noon. Then to hear them. Then his eyes began to glitter in lamplight, and I put a lamp in his lap and watched them go from brown to something like cut quartz. He walked into the sea on the ninth day. I put the splinters in a jar. I have not looked at it since.

maras_kiss_public_house.hook: A bright tavern on the Auridon road with a garden of fruit trees, a lantern for each drinker and a wide stone hearth.
maras_kiss_public_house.rumour: Mara's Kiss serves a cider that sparkles on the tongue. They stopped pouring it after the second drinker went quiet.

notes.title: Cider Ledger
notes.author: Innkeeper Merilin
pages: Barrels pressed: 12. Barrels returned: 11, unopened. Barrel twelve: poured to the last. Patrons affected: 9. Orchard supplier: Shattered Grove, who say it is the best harvest in years and glitter when they speak. I have burned the barrel. The smoke was blue. The splinters were not burned.

shattered_grove.hook: A grove of splintered crystal trees in Auridon, their bark cracked and the fallen fruit sparkling in the grass.
shattered_grove.rumour: The Shattered Grove bore the largest fruit of its life this year. The folk who ate it have all begun to glitter.

notes.title: Wardens' Notice
notes.author: Grove-Warden
pages: DO NOT EAT THE FRUIT. DO NOT TOUCH THE BARK. DO NOT SLEEP UNDER THE BOUGH. A cult has been seen at dusk amongst the splintered trees. They sing, and the grove answers. The wardens have fallen back to the road. Send mages, not soldiers. The trees do not fear blades.

skywatch.hook: A hill-city topped by a vast ring-orrery with concentric stone ring-walks and observatories on each ring.
skywatch.rumour: The great orrery at Skywatch was tilted by a degree one night, and the star-watchers can't say by whom. The conjunction comes sooner now.

notes.title: Star-Watcher's Alarm
notes.author: Star-Watcher Elenwe
pages: The third ring is out of true by one degree. I re-trued it last night and found it tilted again at dawn. Cult marks on the underside: a spiral of tiny crystals. The conjunction is nine weeks away by the old reckoning, and seven by the new. Someone is bringing the seed's waking forward. Send mages.

the_banished_cells.hook: A Daedric prison under a spire with cell-blocks of obsidian, chains and windows on nothing.
the_banished_cells.rumour: A prison under a spire holds those who said no to the fever. They are asking to be let out and they are right.

notes.title: A Prisoner's Smuggled Letter
notes.author: Lyrian Sol
pages: To whom it may concern, I am not mad, I am glass. The seed sings to me but I do not sing back. They keep us because we are proof the fever can be borne. The fortress's heart is a crystal as tall as a man. Break it and the grove will fall silent. I cannot reach it; my legs are no longer mine.

mehrunes_spite.hook: A red-spired fortress of Dagon's cult with lava channels around a central court, spike gardens and a ritual hall under a brazier-crown.
mehrunes_spite.rumour: A red fortress on the Auridon cliffs has a hall where a crystal hums. The cult say it is the future. The grove says otherwise.

notes.title: Cult Hymn
notes.author: the Splinter Court
pages: Break the glass in the heart of the world and let the new light in. Break the heart in the glass of the world and let the old night out. We are the splinters, we are the sharp, we are the ones who do not sleep. Let the grove sing us, let the sea receive us, let the seed be sown.

kings_haven.hook: A small keep and orchard on the Summerset coast, with a reeve's house and a walled egg-yard where gryphon clutches were once gathered.
kings_haven.rumour: The reeve at King's Haven swears the gryphons have stopped laying and then tells you he doesn't believe it.

notes.title: Egg-Tithe Ledger
notes.author: Reeve Ordin
pages: Spring: 30 clutches forwarded to the steward. Summer: 28. Autumn: 31. Winter: 29. Spring this year: 0 laid, 12 stolen from the nest. The steward's receipt says 'received 30, as customary'. There is no customary thirty. The gryphons stopped when the steward's agents first came. I have written to the court. The court has not written back.

the_golden_netch.hook: An inn under a gilded netch-balloon on the Summerset coast road with a rope-ladder entrance and a wide kitchen.
the_golden_netch.rumour: A dealer at the Golden Netch pays for his room in coin and his crates in silence. The crates are warm.

notes.title: Dealer's Bill of Lading
notes.author: Dealer Quorin
pages: To be carried from the Netch to the Shimmerene quay: twelve crates, packed in straw, to remain warm. The steward's seal appears on each. The buyer pays on arrival in Pyandonean coin. Do not shake. Do not let it be said these are eggs. They are 'mineral specimens' on any manifest.

shimmerene.hook: A busy port on a bay with dockside lanterns on high poles, long wharves and crane-masts.
shimmerene.rumour: The quiet quay at Shimmerene has no lantern, and crates marked 'minerals' go aboard a foreign ship after dark. The customs man looks away.

notes.title: Night-Watch Report
notes.author: Watchman Corin
