pages: Quiet quay, third night: seven crates marked 'minerals', warm to the touch, carried aboard a foreign ship under no flag. Customs official seen to turn his back and pocket something. I inquired. I was told the quay was private. A crate had a feather caught in its seam, long as my arm and the colour of the cliffs.

gryphon_aerie.hook: A cliff nest of enormous gryphons on the Summerset coast, ledges of straw and wind-scoured stone.
gryphon_aerie.rumour: The gryphons at the aerie have started calling at night, and their calls are shorter than they used to be.

notes.title: Aerie Warden's Report
notes.author: Warden Syrel
pages: Nests: 40. Occupied: 11. Eggs: 0 laid, 0 hatched. The song has gone thin. I fear for the palace more than for the birds: the stone is tuned to them, and the stone is beginning to tick. If the gryphons stop singing the balconies will fall. If the steward is the cause, I would like to look him in the eye.

cloudrest.hook: A palace-city on a sea cliff with cantilevered balconies over open air, glass floors and no walls.
cloudrest.rumour: Cloudrest hangs its balconies over open air. The steward has been shoring the lower ones with iron where the courtiers will not see.

notes.title: Master-Builder's Report
notes.author: Master-Builder Tolwen
pages: Balcony nine ticks. Balcony eleven ticks and has dropped a hand's breadth. I recommended closing the south wing and was told the steward's office does not recognise the word 'closing'. I have braced the worst of them with iron. The stone was always held by song, and I hear less of it each week.

tor_hame_khard.hook: A crystal fortress carved into a sea cliff with sea-gates at wave level, a waterfall court and a lightning-rod tower.
tor_hame_khard.rumour: The fortress's tower hums at storm-time in a voice like a very large bird.

notes.title: Brooding-Court Plate
pages: HERE THE SONG IS HATCHED AND HERE THE STONE IS TUNED. No palace stands on its own weight; it stands on the voices beneath it. Feed the mothers, warm the clutch, hear the note. If you take the egg, you take the balcony.

trebbite_monastery.hook: A small monastery on the Auridon coast with a cloister of white stone, a silent refectory and an urn of silk spools.
trebbite_monastery.rumour: The Trebbite brothers have found silk in the orchard with words woven in it. They say please don't eat it.

notes.title: Brother Abelar's Notes
notes.author: Brother Abelar
pages: Found in the north cloister: thread, with a word wound in. 'Concerning the tides of Lillandril, a treatise.' A book from the great library, in thread! I do not think it was stolen. I think it was woven, or read aloud and caught. The spiders are the only ones who could have done it. I have left them honey.

dusk.hook: A crescent harbour city under pale dunes, lilac in the evening, with a tall lantern tower and pastel houses.
dusk.rumour: Book-barges come into Dusk at night with cargo that's all blank paper. The bookbinders are doing a brisk trade in covers.

notes.title: Shipping Manifest, Library-Barge
notes.author: Dockmaster Elorin
pages: Barge 'Patience': 400 volumes, water-damaged. Barge 'Quill': 612 volumes, water-damaged. Barge 'Ink': 88 volumes, water-damaged. Inspected: all blank. The librarians cry and the buyers cry. I sealed the manifest. 'Water-damaged' is cheaper than 'devoured'.

lillandril.hook: A city of terraced libraries and observatories on a rock, with ring galleries of book-stacks open to the sky and bronze orreries.
lillandril.rumour: A third of Lillandril's stacks are blank, and the head librarian has gone missing. The assistants say they can hear reading from beyond the cliff.

notes.title: Assistant's Catalogue Note
notes.author: Assistant Faleril
pages: Shelf nine: blank. Shelf ten: blank. Shelf eleven: contents intact, but the dust on the spines is arranged in rows like something walked along it. The head librarian left her tea half-drunk. A silk-thread is tied to the chair. I am not brave. I am the only one who remembers the catalogue. I am writing it all down.

direnni_acropolis.hook: A ruined hilltop acropolis of white columns, a stage of marble and a high cistern of black water.
direnni_acropolis.rumour: The old acropolis has webs across every column, and some say you can hear a voice reading in them.

notes.title: Spider's Verse
notes.author: unknown
pages: ~Weave the word and weave the line,~weave the story into twine.~Eight small hands for a thousand tomes,~eight small hands for the dying homes.~What is read is never lost.~What is spun is worth its cost.

cathedral_of_webs.hook: A crystal vault wrapped in giant spider-silk, shafts of light through white webs onto lecterns of woven thread.
cathedral_of_webs.rumour: The Cathedral of Webs is a place of reading. The spiders sit very still.

notes.title: The Librarian's Diary
notes.author: Head Librarian Sorendil
pages: I came to rescue a book and stayed to hear it read. The spiders do not eat us; they eat nothing but silk and light. They weave the words so they will not be lost. If I stop reading, they stop weaving. I have not stopped. I think I have been reading for a hundred days. I am quite happy.

stay_moist_mansion.hook: A merchant's stilt mansion in the Stormhold marsh with a boat-shed, a bright awning and a lantern-lit veranda.
stay_moist_mansion.rumour: The merchant at Stay-Moist has more sap than a thousand trees could give, and he sells it by the cask to the Imperials.

notes.title: Cask Ledger
notes.author: Factor Delvyn Sull
pages: Casks tapped: 214 this season. Sold to the Imperial pharmacists: 198. Retained for private use: 12. Spoiled: 4. The Root yields well to a determined hand. If the Hist-folk complain, remind them that a tree is not a person. I have never believed in it, but I wouldn't say it aloud in the hearing of the Root.

xal_haj_ei_shrine.hook: A shrine in a hollow reed-forest, half-sunk in a pool, its walls carved with root-patterns.
xal_haj_ei_shrine.rumour: The shrine in the reeds has gone grey. The keepers say the Root is in pain.

notes.title: Keeper's Dawn Prayer
notes.author: Keeper Sa-Heet
pages: Root of the marsh, root of the sky, we are in pain and so are you. A cut is a cut, a tap is a tap, and no one asks the tree. We keep the shrine and we weep, because the shrine weeps. Forgive those who do not know, and those who do. Let the sap run clean.

weeping_wamasu_falls.hook: A high waterfall with the shape of a giant weeping creature carved into the rock behind its sheet.
weeping_wamasu_falls.rumour: The Weeping Wamasu has fallen quiet. The Argonians say it is losing its voice because the marsh has a cut in it.

notes.title: The Wamasu's Elegy
notes.author: unknown Argonian
pages: ~The falls once sang and now they sigh.~The wamasu weeps and the clouds go by.~A root is cut and a throat is sore,~a song unsung is a closing door.~We are the marsh and the marsh is we,~and nobody asked the old Hist tree.

notes.title: The Lullaby of the Last Water
notes.author: the coven
pages: ~Hush, little river, the night is long.~Hush, little spring, I will sing you a song.~Hush, little fall, the tears are deep.~Hush, great mother, and go to sleep.~The world has wept enough, they say.~Close your eyes, and fade away.

temple_of_sul.hook: A sun-temple with bright shafts and a gold altar, its roof carved to focus a single beam at noon.
temple_of_sul.rumour: The Temple of Sul's gold is real, but the priest who kept it hasn't prayed in a year.

notes.title: The Priest's Licence
notes.author: High Priest Thar-Sul
pages: In the name of the sun, the bearer is granted the right to gather sap from the Root at such sites as the bearer chooses, for the sum of three hundred pieces of gold per season. The temple will not be held to account. The sun is a witness, and the sun does not testify.

bogmother.hook: A fetid root-cave and hag-lair where a mother-of-bog spawns, with walls of knotted root and a dripping ceiling.
bogmother.rumour: Something big has been laying in the swamp lately. The hunters won't go past the bend.

notes.title: Hunter's Warning
notes.author: Hunter Ta-Shu
pages: Do not go near the bend. Her spawn come in clutches of nine now, where it was three. She is enraged, and she has cause. Whoever put the pipe through her ceiling should be fed to the next clutch. I will not go in. I have children.

shrine_of_the_black_maw.hook: A sacred shrine built into a gaping rock mouth with processional halls and a great black pool.
shrine_of_the_black_maw.rumour: The Black Maw's pool has a metal thing in it now. The shrine-keepers say it is a thorn in the world's tongue.

notes.title: The Maw's Lip
pages: WHAT IS DRAWN RETURNS, WHAT IS TAKEN IS OWED. The Root remembers every hand that touched it. Draw not what is not yours; and if you have drawn it, return it threefold. The black water is patient, but it is not blind.

hatchlings_crown.hook: A hill crowned with a ring of egg-shaped stones near Lilmoth, each carved with a notch-count of warmth.
hatchlings_crown.rumour: The egg-stones of the crown measure the warmth of the pools. The last cut is the deepest anyone has seen.

notes.title: Egg-Keeper's Count
notes.author: Egg-Keeper Ushu
pages: Count at dawn: 92 degrees. Last year: 94. The year before: 96. The eggs hatch pale now, and some do not hatch. A degree each year for ten years. I have asked the Hist-sages. They say the heat has been called elsewhere, and nobody called it. I have a strong suspicion. I will not say it aloud.

hatching_pools.hook: A ring of warm pools in Stormhold's lowland, each steaming faintly with a clutch in a nest of reeds.
hatching_pools.rumour: The hatching pools are cooler. The steam goes south in a thread, and the keepers follow it with their eyes.

notes.title: Pool-Keeper's Report
notes.author: Keeper Sh-Thissa
pages: Pool one: 88 degrees, was 90. Pool two: 87, was 89. Steam goes south. I followed it to the wall of Lilmoth and lost it among the market stalls. I do not think the market is the thief. I think the thief is further. The steam is a thread, and a thread may be followed.

the_vile_pavilion.hook: A rotting banquet pavilion on the mire with floating platforms joined by plank walks and a long table with plates that still steam.
the_vile_pavilion.rumour: A pavilion in the mire has food that steams on a night with frost. Nobody who sits there has returned for dessert.

notes.title: An Invitation, Late
notes.author: The Lord of the Long Supper
pages: My dear guest: you are late, and the soup has gone cold, but I have made it warm again. Sit. Eat. We have been so long without company. The plates were set at the turn of the season, and the season turned eighteen times. I am so sorry about the weather. Do not leave before the sweets.

jeevu_rice_paddy.hook: A rice paddy in the Shadowfen, with rows of seedlings in black water and a harvest-counter's high chair.
jeevu_rice_paddy.rumour: The rice-counter at Jeevu counts forty-two at dusk where there were forty-one at dawn. She doesn't like it.

notes.title: Rice-Counter's Tally
notes.author: Counter Sheena
pages: Dawn count: 41. Dusk count: 42. Bowls set: 42. Bowls emptied: 42. I do not feed one extra worker. I feed forty-one and the forty-second bowl is emptied by morning. The harvest has been good, and I will not question what labours in the dark. But I count, and the count does not lie.

root_whisper_village.hook: An abandoned Hist-village, huts overgrown with root-vine and a central fire-pit still warm at the edges.
root_whisper_village.rumour: Root Whisper's folk left in a night. The roots have grown into their huts and their table has a chair that stays warm.

notes.title: A Villager's Last Diary
notes.author: Uziah of Root Whisper
pages: The root spoke, three nights running. A name, nothing more. We could not hear it exactly, but we knew it was a name. We began to set a place. The elders thought it was an ancestor. The children said no. It was someone who had never been counted. The thirteenth night, the root said it again, and we left. I am sorry.

notes.title: Ash-Song
notes.author: unknown
pages: ~From the red hill to the green,~from the mountain to the mire,~ash goes drifting, ash is seen,~ash goes carrying its fire.~What it burned it will not lose.~What it knew it will not choose.~In the root, the ash is heard,~each name a quiet, rooted word.

ruins_of_mazzatun.hook: A xanmeer of stepped chambers where the floor is a flooded city, with sap-vein walls and a central shaft.
ruins_of_mazzatun.rumour: Mazzatun's flood rises a hand per year. Folk say a quiet figure sits at the bottom and counts.

notes.title: The Founder's Wall
pages: HE WHO WAS FIRST HAS NO NAME BECAUSE NONE WAS GIVEN. He built the first hut, and the first fire. He wished to be counted and was not. Let whoever finds this give him a name of the marsh, and let it be a good one.

hutan_tzel.hook: A fishing hamlet on the southern delta, with drying racks and a graveyard whose markers are wooden reeds.
hutan_tzel.rumour: At Hutan Tzel the dead are buried inland, now. The singers don't sing them to the water.

notes.title: A Fisher's Plea
notes.author: Fisher Lutha
pages: To the Grave-Singers: my father was not sung to the water. He lies in a field that is not ours, in a place that will be dry within a year. Please. The dirge is the only road he has and it has been closed. Someone has money in the Gideon fields and my father has been sold for rain.

grave_singers_lodge.hook: A lodge of singers on a hummock in the delta, hung with reed-chimes, with a single long table of seven empty chairs.
grave_singers_lodge.rumour: The singers' lodge has seven chairs and three singers. The other four have taken the lord's coin.

notes.title: The Old Verse
notes.author: the Grave-Singers
pages: ~Down the delta, down the water,~sing the sons and sing the daughters.~Past the reeds and past the flood,~to the teeth that drink the blood.~Lay them where the tide is slow.~Sing them home. We'll sing them so.

plateau_of_the_traveler.hook: A lone rock plateau with a view across the delta and a flat stone, polished by feet, at its edge.
plateau_of_the_traveler.rumour: From the lone plateau you can see two paths. One is silver, one is dark. Choose carefully which you follow.

notes.title: Surveyor's Sighting
notes.author: Surveyor Haleth
pages: At dusk the old route shines like a fish's back down to the sea. The new route runs due east through the drier fields of Gideon. The two paths part at a mound near the third marsh-bend. I walked the new route. It ended in a plantation courtyard with a bell. The bell was silent, and the courtyard was full of coffins waiting.

teeth_of_sithis.hook: A ring of black teeth rising from the mire around a sunken hollow, with root paths between each tooth, each tooth a different trial.
teeth_of_sithis.rumour: The ring of teeth is quiet. The old folk say it used to sing.

notes.title: The Tooth Inscription
pages: WHEN THE DIRGE IS SUNG THE TEETH ARE QUIET. WHEN THE DIRGE IS LOST THE TEETH ARE HUNGRY. Sing the dead down the water. Do not sell the road. Do not bend the song. The teeth are patient but they are not kind.

saarvik_landing.hook: A landing of broken ships on an Atmoran shore, ribs and masts half-buried in drifts, a single cairn at the tide line.
saarvik_landing.rumour: At Saarvik the ships sit in drifts, and the cairn's rune glows when the ice speaks.

notes.title: The Cairn Rune
pages: ICE CRACKS UNDER THE LONG HALLS. WHO HAS EARS, HEAR IT. The ships here were broken by those who chose not to leave. Do not make their choice. The captain's ship waits in the howe. Wake her before the thaw.

skjaldborg.hook: A shield-fort on the Atmoran ice, its wall a ring of battered shields and a single hall of frosted wood.
skjaldborg.rumour: The shields at Skjaldborg all face the ice now. The captain won't say who turned them.

notes.title: Shield-Captain's Last Page
notes.author: Captain Ragnhild
pages: The ice is groaning at night; the seam runs under the halls of Kjolvik and out to sea. The old chiefs swore to keep the howe's ship, but nobody has been to the howe in three generations. Send word to the hold. Tell them the dragon-mound is the pin. If the pin goes, the shelf goes.

kjolvik.hook: A last Atmoran hold on an ice shelf with ten long halls half-buried in drifts, whale-bone arches and a stone-lined harbour where ice cracks.
kjolvik.rumour: Kjolvik's elders sing in the long hall at night, loudly, so the ice cannot be heard. The children ask to be taught the old ship-songs.

notes.title: A Child's Letter to the Shield-Fort
notes.author: Tove of Kjolvik
pages: To the Captain: the ice is talking again. The grown-ups sing to cover it. I counted the cracks in the harbour and there are forty-one now. Papa says not to count. Nana says to count and to pack. We have packed sledges and left them by the door. Please send the captain of the howe's ship if there is one.

the_frozen_dragon_mound.hook: A mound of ice with a dragon's head frozen at its crown, jaws open in a final roar.
the_frozen_dragon_mound.rumour: The frozen dragon has begun to weep at the throat, and the ice-seam under the halls is following it.

notes.title: Chief's Last Oath-Notes
notes.author: Chief Vigdis
pages: The head is the pin and the pin must hold. If it thaws, the shelf will break, and the hold will drift out to sea in ten halves. We swore to keep the howe's ship ready for such a day. Ready, I say, as if we had ever opened her gate. The oath is an old man's boast. Wake the ship, whoever comes.

notes.title: Hold-Chief's Warning
notes.author: Chief Vigdis
pages: A foreign man came to the mound last year in a cloak of red silk. He cut a bone from the dragon's throat while it slept, and the dragon, which had not stirred in a thousand years, shuddered. The ice began to crack that night. Do not let any who wear red silk near the mound.

wolf_jarls_howe.hook: A great Atmoran barrow under a hill of snow with a long ship buried whole as the dungeon's central room.
wolf_jarls_howe.rumour: The howe's ship is whole. They say you can hear her creak in the dark of the barrow.

notes.title: The Prow-Stone
pages: SHE SLEEPS TO CARRY US HOME. The word is the name of the hold, spoken as a promise. When the ice breaks, wake the ship. When the ship wakes, board her. Do not look back at the shelf. It was only ever a place to wait.

notes.title: A Wolf-Jarl's Last Letter
notes.author: Wolf-Jarl Ottar
pages: To my heirs: I have the crown of the foreign king beneath the keel of my ship and I will carry it to my own grave rather than let it go to any living man. It is a heavy thing. It weighs nothing. It does not shine. I will not look at it. Bury me on top of it, and do not ask why my sleep is so poor.

tang_mo_watch.hook: A border watchtower on the Tang Mo coast with a lantern at its crown and a stone at its foot carved with a fourfold seal.
tang_mo_watch.rumour: The watchmen say the border stone has been rubbed smooth by pilgrims, all but one corner that stays cold.

notes.title: Watch Orders
notes.author: Watch-Captain Chen
pages: Do not let pilgrims chip the stone. The fourth quarter is cold. Do not touch it with bare hands. Send word to the harbour that the seal's strength fails by a quarter per generation. The court that holds the last has not answered in two hundred years. Keep the lantern lit.

tang_mo_harbor_village.hook: A harbour of lacquered junks and floating lantern-masts, houses raised on bamboo piles with curved roofs and a dragon-prowed ship at the quay.
tang_mo_harbor_village.rumour: The dragon-prow at Tang Mo's quay has a jade tablet set in its throat that glows when the tide is high. The ferrymen have a seal tattooed on their palms.

notes.title: Ferryman's Journal
notes.author: Ferryman Wen
pages: Tide high: the jade glows. Tide low: it sleeps. My grandfather's palm bore the same mark as mine, a quarter-circle with a notch. We carry the harbour's quarter of the seal, though none of us knows what it seals. A monk once asked to read it. I let him. He wept, and took nothing. It is a heavy thing to keep and a heavier thing to lose.

tiger_plains_village.hook: A mountain village of curved-roof pagodas on rice terraces with a vermilion shrine gate, bamboo and paper lanterns.
tiger_plains_village.rumour: A lantern in the headman's house at Tiger Plains has burned without oil since before the village had a name, and he says it is a family heirloom.

notes.title: Headman's Lantern Note
notes.author: Headman Li
pages: The lantern was lit by my ancestor's ancestor and has never gone out. In the rain, in the wind, in the long dark of the third winter. It is set in a quarter-circle of jade that does not match any craftsman's art. A traveller offered a great sum. I told him it was not mine to sell. I did not tell him it was not mine to keep.

temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.hook: A tall serpent-roofed temple on a Tsaesci ridge, with coils of painted stair and a bell-gate at the summit.
temple_of_the_serpent_emperor.rumour: The serpent-priests wait. They wait without hurry, and they are not the ones who fear.

notes.title: Priests' Patient Prayer
notes.author: the Tsaesci priests
pages: Three have bowed, one waits. Let the emperor's coil close upon the last. We are patient: we were patient in the ice and patient in the fire. We will be patient until the fourth is brought to us in a cold hand. Great coil, great hunger, great quiet.

notes.title: The Spine-Cradle Plate
pages: FORTY-ONE FOR THE LADDER, FORTY-ONE FOR THE CLIMB. When the last is set the court will rise. We have waited a thousand years. We can wait for two more bones, and a quiet that does not end.

dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.hook: A valley floor of enormous ribcages, white as salt under a low sky, with a path of vertebrae winding between them.
dragon_graveyard_of_akavir.rumour: The valley of ribs groans at dusk. The Akaviri say it is the dragons turning over in their sleep.

notes.title: Dirge of the Valley
notes.author: unknown
pages: ~We came to die where the north wind breathes,~we came to lie where the ice-flower seethes.~Rib by rib and wing by wing,~we left our names to the silent thing.~If you would wake us, bring the four.~If you would sleep, then close the door.

frost_throne_of_kamal.hook: A throne-hall of ice and iron with a giant ice throne in a hall of ice pagodas.
frost_throne_of_kamal.rumour: The throne of Kamal is cold even in summer. The frost-warden has not blinked in a thousand years.

notes.title: The Throne's Arm
pages: FOUR COURTS, FOUR QUARTERS, ONE SEAL. Whoever joins them keeps the valley shut. Whoever breaks them opens it. It is the warden's duty to ask which you choose, and to remember.

notes.title: The Throne's Last Socket
pages: THE EIGHTH PIECE SITS HERE: THE ARM THAT HELD THE SCEPTRE. He who sets the ring, the crown, the sceptre and the sword in their places makes the king whole, and the king will rise, and the king will remember who he was. There is no one left who remembers who he was. This is the mercy.

serpent_pens.hook: A serpent pen of coral-walled pools on a Maormer isle, with feeding platforms and pole-and-net gates.
serpent_pens.rumour: The serpents at the pens eat a pink weed and grow, and one pen has already burst. The keepers don't speak of it.

notes.title: Pen-Keeper's Report
notes.author: Pen-Keeper Isaal
pages: Pen 4: burst. Pen 7: bloated, one dead. Pen 9: normal, but the coral grows through the gate. The coral is from the Thras sea; it drifts. I fed them on it because the fish run is poor. They are bigger. They are hungrier. I do not think the coral is food. I think it is an invitation.

notes.title: Maormer Pen-Keeper's Letter
notes.author: Pen-Keeper Isaal
pages: To the admiral: a page of the Yokudan ledger has come into my keeping. It was in the totem's hollow. I am told it is the fifth of nine. I do not know what it is for. It seems to be tides. If it is valuable, I would like an honest price. If it is dangerous, I would like it taken away.

pyandonean_fleet_anchorage.hook: A fleet at anchor, a raft-city of shell-hulled ships lashed together, a coral flagship and serpent-prowed boats, gleaming wet.
pyandonean_fleet_anchorage.rumour: The shell-hulled fleet at anchor keeps pulling south against its lashings. The admiral says it is the current. The deck-hands do not.

notes.title: Quartermaster's Drift Report
notes.author: Quartermaster Hesh
pages: Fleet drift: four fathoms south-east since the last tide. Lashings tightened nightly. Anchor chain of the flagship: strained. The current does not run that way. I took a pink coral-shard from the flagship's keel; it was warm, and moved a little in my palm when the fleet turned. The admiral says it is a trick of the water. I say the water has a will.

coral_tower_of_thras.hook: A tower of living coral in a sea of plague, with rooms of pulsing polyps, bright pink and poison green and a spiral reef stair.
coral_tower_of_thras.rumour: The tower in the plague sea has grown a fathom this year. The folk of Thras say it is thinking.

notes.title: A Diver's Last Entry
notes.author: Diver Moraleth
pages: The tower breathes. I did not believe it, but there it is: each room expands and contracts. The heart is down below, a thing like a lung the size of a house. It is not ill. It is not mad. It is simply patient, and it wants to be larger. It does not know there is a fleet. It does not know there is a shore. It only knows 'more'.

orgnums_citadel.hook: A sea-serpent citadel on a crag with boat-lifts, brine tanks, serpent pens and a throne hall with a window onto the deep.
orgnums_citadel.rumour: The sea-king stares into the deep and will not eat. The court says he is waiting for it to blink.

notes.title: A Counsellor's Letter
notes.author: Counsellor Veshra
pages: My lord does not sleep. He has stood at the great window since the reef came within sight. I fear he will go out to it. Some say he should: that it is a gift from the sea. Others say it is a plague. I say it does not matter what it is: we cannot hold it, and we cannot feed it, and we have not the sense to leave.

notes.title: The Window Frame
pages: THE SIXTH PAGE LOOKS ON THE DEEP. The sea-king keeps it where his gaze may rest upon it. He says it is a map to a place he does not wish to visit. If you take it, he will know. If you do not, he will wonder, and wondering is how kingdoms fall.

ra_gada_encampment.hook: A camp on the Yokudan desert's edge, sand-coloured tents, a drill-yard and a training-post carved with four forms.
ra_gada_encampment.rumour: At the Ra Gada camp they will tell you the fourth form is taught on the water, and then they stop speaking.

notes.title: Drill-Master's Notes
notes.author: Master Baradi
pages: Four forms: the Wave, the Wind, the Stone, the Return. The first three I taught in this yard. The fourth is a thing the old masters said could only be taught on the water, to one who has learnt the others. None has learnt. The last student drowned. The sandal is his. I keep it, as one keeps a lesson not yet finished.

notes.title: Drill-Master's Page-Note
notes.author: Master Baradi
pages: A seventh page, nailed under the lesson-post by a hand I did not see. I have no wish to read it. It is the property of the kings, not the camp. The final two pages lie beyond the water, in a place where the kings sleep. If you mean to read the ledger, you must first complete the Last Lesson.

hundings_dojo.hook: A sunken courtyard dojo on a Yokudan island with a bowl of sand, a ring of columns, tiers of benches and a single bright pavilion.
hundings_dojo.rumour: The sand bowl at Hunding's dojo is raked in a spiral every dawn. The master bows to an empty bench and no one has told him it is empty.

notes.title: Master's Teaching Notes
notes.author: Master Yazid
pages: Students this year: none. Students last year: two, both gone before the second form. The second form is the Wind, which cannot be taught on land. It is learned on the shore, when the tide is going out. I will bow to the empty bench until one fills it. I am old, and the sand does not tire, and the lesson is not yet finished.

temple_of_satakal.hook: A temple to the world-eater snake on an island, its roof a great coil and its floor a mosaic of scales.
temple_of_satakal.rumour: The temple's priests teach a dance on a floor of scales. They say it ends where it should.

notes.title: The Scale Floor
pages: WHO DANCES HERE DANCES TOWARD THE MOUTH. The world-eater is patient, the world-eater is kind in its way. Dance, and be swallowed, and be returned. The fourth form is taught on the water. The snake is the water's friend.

sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.hook: A sunken sea-temple of flooded halls, coral shelves and air pockets, with a king's funeral barge filling the central hall and walls carved with a voyage.
sunken_temple_of_the_yokudan_kings.rumour: The sunken temple's barge has never left. The Ra Gada say it is waiting for someone who has finished their lessons.

notes.title: The Rower's Verse
notes.author: the Ra Gada
pages: ~The Wave, the Wind, the Stone, the Return.~The first you learn and the last you earn.~Row, row, the barge is old,~the kings are heavy, the water cold.~But a hand on the oar and a heart that is true~will carry the lesson, and the kings, home too.

notes.title: The Barge's Deck
pages: NINE PAGES, NINE PORTS, NINE HANDS. The road home is not a place but a tide, and it comes but once in each age. Read it aloud and the barge will sail. Burn it, and the kings will sleep. The tide does not care which you choose.
